Fontaine/History (also: History of Fontaine, Fontaine Timeline, Fontainian History): Fontaine's past runs from the Primordial Sea, the source of all life, ruled in the Old World by the Hydro Dragon Sovereign. The Heavenly Principles took that Authority and made Egeria the sea's new heart. The god Remus founded the musical empire of Remuria, which sank about 2,000 years ago, and Egeria then became Hydro Archon. Her act of giving Oceanids human form was branded a sin and a prophecy of dissolving floods followed. Egeria died in the Cataclysm about 500 years ago; her successor Focalors spent five centuries on a plan that ended in Version 4.2, when the prophecy was fulfilled in form and defused in fact.

Use this entry to place events in order and give rough "how long ago". Order of eras: Old World, the Heavenly Principles take the Hydro Authority, the great flood that ends the first era, Remuria (Archon War period), Egeria's rule, the Cataclysm and Focalors' succession, the Melusines and Neuvillette's appointment, the Recent Past, and the resolution of the prophecy in 4.2. For the underlying mysteries defer to the prophecy, Egeria, Focalors and Remuria entries.

Old world: In the Seven Sovereigns' era the Primordial Sea lay on the world's surface. Most of Teyvat's life traces back to it, and the Hydro Dragon Sovereign was its "beating heart".

The Hydro Dragon is sometimes called the original god of life, and the sea its "birthing waters" or "amniotic fluid". Life within the Primordial Sea was a collective rather than separate individuals. The wiki treats these as lore statements from item and book text, not dated events.

First era flood: Near the end of what a Remurian history calls the "first era", likely the unified civilisation, humanity began to covet what belonged to Celestia and to resist its fate. Cities were destroyed by tsunamis and buried after 100 days of rain that "drowned all sin and arrogation"; humanity had to rebuild. The envoy Sybilla, who guarded an Irminsul tree, survived as the only one left from that age.

Egeria and the oceanids: The wiki places this in the interim between the great wars. Egeria's first tear is said to have given birth to the first Oceanid, and the Oceanids were told to understand every kind of creature and to love them. They spread across Teyvat's waters as watchers. When some of them longed to live on the surface among humans, Egeria took Primordial Seawater and poured it into their vessels, giving them humanoid forms. Celestia judged this an unauthorised creation of life, a sin, and sentenced her to be sealed. Fontaine's people learned of a prophecy that the waters would rise and dissolve them, washing away the sin.

Remuria: Some time after Gurabad fell in Sumeru, the god Remus came to the High Seas looking for a place to die and found a forgotten city whose last inhabitants were Sybilla and the other Golden Bees. They told him he would found a prosperous nation whose desire for justice would doom it. Remus accepted, the Irminsul became a golden ship, and he established the empire of Remuria over the waters. Its golden age brought agriculture, great cities and temples, music and art. He called other tribes into the empire through the Fortuna and conquered those who refused, such as the tribe of Erinnyes and Cassiodor. Worried by the prophecy of its fall, Remus went to Egeria's prison in the Primordial Sea; Scylla, her guardian, fought him for thirty days and nights before letting him pass. Egeria could not help, but gave him a goblet of primordial water, and Scylla left the sea to join his cause.

Egeria archon: After Remuria sank, Celestia ordered Egeria out of her prison to take Remus' place. She gathered the survivors, settled their feuds, and told them to found new cities around flowing springs, beginning an era of law that lasts to the present. She received a Gnosis, became the Hydro Archon, and one of the Seven. After the Archon War she travelled to Liyue for the gatherings of the original Seven. She exiled criminals from her nation; those who begged forgiveness she heard in the waters, and she ordered them to guard her secret, the way to the Primordial Sea, from beneath the waves. That led to the Fortress of Meropide, whose real purpose was later forgotten.

Cataclysm and succession: About 500 years ago Egeria died fighting the Abyss at Tunigi Hollow in the Cataclysm, and Focalors took over. The Oceanids refused to obey Focalors and left Fontaine on self-imposed exile; Fontaine's waters turned bitter. In Sumeru the wiki reports that Egeria's body became the pure waters of the Amrita. The same period saw the great beast Elynas spreading pollution; the retired admiral Basil Elton led the Fontaine Armada in a 35-day pursuit and rammed it, destroying the fleet and mortally wounding Elynas, who died while keeping consciousness. A great flood, the first diluvian period, submerged much of Fontaine including the Narzissenkreuz Institute, which closed.

Focalors plan: About 499 years before the Masquerade of the Guilty, Focalors separated her divinity from her body and spirit; the human she left behind was Furina, who took the public role of Hydro Archon. Focalors then sealed herself in the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale as its verdict-giving mind. Trials at the Opera Epiclese produced Indemnitium from public belief in justice. A small share powered Fontaine; the rest was stored for the day the prophecy's trial of the Hydro Archon was held. Focalors also kept the Hydro Gnosis with her divine half and cursed Furina to live as long as Focalors existed, without chasing her own happiness.

Melusines and neuvillette: About 400 years ago Neuvillette became Iudex. In the same period the Melusines were born from wounds in Elynas' remains, caused by shrapnel from an explosion of destroyed clockwork meka during the Marechaussee operation against the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. Neuvillette brought them into the rest of Fontaine, where many people distrusted them, partly because of "strange incidents" and his own fresh appointment.

Recent past: The "Two Musketeers" incident: an assassin hired by Morris killed Elisa to hide an illegitimate relationship; their children Baptiste and Veronique witnessed it and sought revenge. About three years before the story, Callas, president of the Spina di Rosula and Navia's father, was accused of murdering the double agent Jacques; he chose a duel over a trial and died at Clorinde's hands, asking her to look after Navia. Wriothesley was adopted into a trafficking scheme, killed the couple and freed the children, was sent to Meropide and later took over as its administrator by winning a duel against the previous administrator.

Present day: In the Archon Quest the prophecy comes true on the day Furina is put on trial before the people, Neuvillette and the Oratrice and judged guilty; the Oratrice sentences "the Hydro Archon". A giant whale, the All-Devouring Narwhal, breaks into the Opera Epiclese and Childe holds it back. Focalors executes herself with the stored Indemnitium, destroying the Hydro Archon's throne and freeing Furina from her curse. Neuvillette, with the Hydro Authority fully his, forgives all Fontainians their original sin and makes them true humans, so the Primordial Sea can no longer dissolve them. In the battle against the Narwhal, the flood foretold by the prophecy arrives but recedes as quickly; those already dissolved are not restored, and the Wingalet rescues many from drowning.

Accounts: The Oceanids' account (Egeria made them by a tear and Celestia punished her) differs from later researchers' view on who created them. Neuvillette reports rumours that the prophecy is rooted in Egeria's last words before her death; the words themselves are not recorded. Remurian history comes mostly from The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria, written a century after the fall.

Open questions: How long Fontaine's civilisation existed before Remuria, the prophecy's true author, how the Golden Troupe relates to Jakob, and whether Egeria survives in any form are not resolved in Fontaine's story. Do not date items the wiki leaves loose.

Connections: This history ties into the Master Timeline, Khaenri'ah's history (the Cataclysm and the Ordo's ruins), and Sumeru through Gurabad, Remus' origin and the Harvisptokhm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the prophecy is resolved, the Hydro Archon's throne is destroyed, there is no Hydro Archon, Neuvillette is Chief Justice and Furina lives as an ordinary person. No later Fontaine upheaval is recorded in the sources used. In 6.7 the Harbinger Sandrone was revived at the Fontaine Research Institute and reappeared in public during a Fontinalia Festival before returning to Snezhnaya (see the sub-entry).

1.comment: Fontaine/History: Original Sin and the Prophecy of Fontaine
1.content: Fontaine's people are said to be born with an original sin: the unauthorised creation of humans from Oceanids by Egeria. The prophecy says the waters will rise, those with sin will dissolve, and only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping on her throne. Stone slates south of Poisson show the stages. In Version 4.2 it was fulfilled in form, with a trial and a flood, but defused in fact when Neuvillette absolved the people.

2.content: Remus' empire sank about 2,000 years ago after he turned his people's souls into stone-bodied golems, built Phobos from Sybilla's life, and conspired with Scylla to destroy it; the Harmost Boethius sealed Scylla and the empire drowned. The ruins now lie in the Sea of Bygone Eras.

3.content: Egeria ruled from about 2,000 to 500 years ago, founded Fontaine's law, and exiled criminals who later built the Fortress of Meropide over the path to the Primordial Sea. She died at Tunigi Hollow in the Cataclysm and named Focalors her successor.

4.content: Focalors split her divinity from Furina, hid in the Oratrice, stored Indemnitium from the Opera Epiclese's trials, and executed herself in 4.2 to destroy the Hydro Archon's throne and return the Authority to Neuvillette.

5.comment: Fontaine/History: Melusines and the Medal of Peace
5.content: About 400 years ago the Melusine Carole and Vautrin of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol earned the Medal of Peace for improving relations between species. Hardliners framed Carole and she took her own life; Vautrin avenged her, was exiled to Meropide and founded the Mutual Aid Society.

6.content: About three years before the story, Callas chose a duel against Clorinde rather than endanger Navia by testifying against Sinthe producers, after being accused of murdering Jacques. He asked Clorinde to look after Navia.

7.content:
History of Inazuma (also: Inazuma History, Inazuma/History, Inazuma timeline, history of the Inazuma archipelago): Inazuma's recorded history runs from islands flooded after the War of Funerary Flame, through the Archon War, when Ei (the Raiden Shogun) conquered the archipelago and slew Orobashi, to the Cataclysm 500 years ago, when her twin Makoto died in Khaenri'ah. Grieving, Ei spent centuries pursuing "Eternity" through a puppet Shogun while she meditated in the Plane of Euthymia. Under Fatui influence the Shogunate issued the Sakoku and Vision Hunt decrees about a year before the Traveler arrived. The Traveler helped end both, and Inazuma is open and quiet as of 7.1.

Use this entry for "what came before what" in Inazuma. For depth on a single episode (the Vision Hunt, the Tatarigami, the Byakuyakoku, the Thunderbird) defer to that episode's own entry. The sequence below follows the wiki's editor-assembled chronology, so round dates are approximate.

Unified civilization and funerary flame: In the oldest era the Inazuma region belonged to a single human civilisation. Enkanomiya (Byakuyakoku) was part of it, as was a Celestia-linked people on Tsurumi Island who worshipped the Three Moons and a sand-built kingdom north of Narukami Island. A great Electro eagle, later called the Thunderbird (Kapatcir), was also born. The War of Funerary Flame killed the Three Moons, and a flood swept Inazuma, leaving few islands.

Enkanomiya and interim: After the war, Enkanomiya's people prayed to the Heavenly Principles and were answered only by Istaroth. A sage called Abrax (Aberaku) built the Dainichi Mikoshi as an artificial sun to drive off the vishaps. Nobles later made the Sunchild a puppet ruler.

Archon war in inazuma: Ei conquered many youkai races; they helped humans reach the mountains and build a city by the sea, which was Inazuma's beginning. More than 2,000 years ago she killed the gods she had defeated and united the islands. She believed her twin Makoto the better ruler, gave up her body so Makoto could ascend to Celestia, and became her kagemusha. Most of Teyvat came to believe there was a single god, Baal, the Raiden Shogun.

Tsurumi and seirai: On Tsurumi Island a man named Ruu befriended the Thunderbird, who had forgotten her own name; he offered her "Kanna Kapatcir". After Ruu was sacrificed in a misguided rite, she destroyed his people and the island relived its last day under a ley line disorder. On Seirai Island she was later killed by Ei about 1,500 years ago.

Cataclysm and ei eternity: Around 500 years ago the Cataclysm struck. Makoto left Ei to defend Inazuma and went alone to Khaenri'ah, where she was killed; Ei found her dying and carried her consciousness home. The Sacred Sakura appeared on Mt. Yougou and helped Ei end the monster crisis. Ei, shattered, resolved to find Eternity.

Tatarasuna and gokaden: Ei's first prototype puppet woke in Shakkei Pavilion and lived among Tatarasuna's smiths as "Kabukimono". In the Tatarasuna incident, Il Dottore (as Escher) poisoned the town with Tatarigami; the puppet came to hate gods and humans and later took the name Kunikuzushi (Scaramouche, the Wanderer).

Recent past to present: About a year before the Traveler arrived, the Fatui steered the Tenryou and Kanjou commissions, the Shogun issued the Sakoku Decree to close the borders and the Vision Hunt Decree to seize Visions, and the Sangonomiya Resistance rose. The Traveler, Yae Miko and the Watatsumi Army had the Vision Hunt abolished; a ceasefire followed and Sakoku was lifted after Transient Dreams.

8.comment: History of Inazuma: Orobashi and the Yashiori War
8.content: Orobashi, the sea serpent god of Watatsumi, fled the Archon War, took in Enkanomiya's people and made Watatsumi Island from coral grown from his body. Famine drove him to invade Yashiori Island with Akuou, Mouun and Ayame. After Akuou killed the Great Tengu Sasayuri, Ei struck down Orobashi and Akuou with Musou no Hitotachi. His lingering resentment became the Tatarigami, held back by Narukami Pillars.

9.comment: History of Inazuma: Makoto's death and the Sacred Sakura
9.content: Makoto, Ei's twin and the first Electro Archon, went alone to Khaenri'ah during the Cataclysm and died in Ei's arms. Ei took her consciousness back to Inazuma, where the Sacred Sakura appeared on Mt. Yougou and helped end the crisis. Ei, who had been Makoto's kagemusha, took Makoto's place as the world's only known Electro Archon.

10.content: Roughly 400 years ago, Il Dottore, posing as the Fontaine mechanic Escher, modified the Mikage Furnace and released Tatarigami, poisoning Tatarasuna and killing the armory officer Niwa. Ei's first prototype puppet, called Kabukimono, believed the Shogunate had abandoned them. He later called himself Kunikuzushi.

11.comment: History of Inazuma: Sakoku and the Vision Hunt
11.content: About a year before the Traveler's arrival, Fatui influence over the Tenryou and Kanjou commissions led the Shogun to close Inazuma's borders and seize Visions. The Watatsumi Army resisted and a stalemate followed. The Traveler and Yae Miko ended the Vision Hunt; Sakoku lapsed after Transient Dreams.

12.comment: History of Inazuma: Thunderbird and Ruu
12.content: Ruu befriended the forgetful Thunderbird by singing and named her Kanna Kapatcir. When he was sacrificed she massacred his tribe and trapped Tsurumi in a repeating day, then devastated Seirai until Ei killed her on Amakumo Peak. The Traveler later helped Ruu's spirit keep his promise.

13.content:
Khaenri'ah/History (also: History of Khaenri'ah, Khaenri'ahn history, Khaenriah history, Kingdom of Khaenri'ah history): Khaenri'ah was a godless nation built underground beneath what is now the Sumeru desert, founded about 6,000 years ago and later ruled by two dynasties, the Crimson Moon and then the Eclipse. About 500 years ago its last king, Irmin, pursued Abyssal power. Five of his greatest subjects, the Five Sinners, seized that power, the Abyss poured into Teyvat, and the gods and the Heavenly Principles destroyed the kingdom. Its pure-blooded survivors were cursed with immortality and still wander the world.

The history runs in rough order: founding, the Crimson Moon Dynasty, the coup that brought the Eclipse Dynasty, the long build-up of machines and forbidden knowledge, Irmin's reign and the Traveler's sibling's arrival, the palace raid and the Five Sinners, the Cataclysm and the evacuation to Sumeru, and then the survivors' scattered story (the Abyss Order, the Fatui, Kaeya, Arlecchino, Dainsleif) through 7.1. Canon never gives a full sequence of the Cataclysm, so many links are the wiki's reconstruction.

Irmin and the sibling: More than 500 years ago Vedrfolnir was born, and later his younger brother Dainsleif. Irmin ascended the throne, and his most trusted advisers became Hroptatyr and Vedrfolnir, with Rhinedottir, Surtalogi, Rerir and Dainsleif rising to prestige as well. The Traveler and their sibling fell to Teyvat in their ship after their home world was destroyed and were separated. The sibling woke first, searched for the Traveler, reached Khaenri'ah and was declared Irmin's heir and "Savior", Princess or Prince of Khaenri'ah. Shortly after, Irmin used the sibling as a vessel to absorb "unlimited Abyssal power".

Five sinners and the raid: When Dainsleif heard of Vedrfolnir's imprisonment he led a rescue that was also a coup, with Rerir, Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir and Surtalogi. Irmin triggered secret mechanisms that attracted Abyssal monsters to the palace. Rerir saw Tholindis flee through a portal, rejoined the group and, with Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir, Surtalogi and Vedrfolnir, divided the Abyssal energy the sibling had absorbed, one-sixth each. They gained "world-shattering" power and became the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah. Dainsleif claims that together with the five he could have stopped Irmin.

Cataclysm: About 500 years ago Abyssal monsters, including creations of Rhinedottir such as the dragon Durin, poured out of Khaenri'ah across all seven nations. The Heavenly Principles and the gods destroyed Khaenri'ah for its use of forbidden knowledge. Ronova, the Ruler of Death, cursed all pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns with immortality, which ends death and aging but not erosion. Dainsleif was cursed too, and keeps a ring from Vedrfolnir that resets his body but not the erosion of his mind. The sibling saw Khaenri'ah fall, woke the Traveler, and tried to leave Teyvat but was stopped by Asmoday, who separated and sealed them.

Post cataclysm and survivors: Both the Crimson Moon Dynasty and the Alberich Clan survived and produced descendants such as Arlecchino and Kaeya. Pierro, embittered at the world's foundational principles, met the Cryo Archon and co-founded the Fatui. Over 100 years ago, after the events of Caribert, Chlothar Alberich founded the Abyss Order to avenge Khaenri'ah on Celestia and the Seven. The sibling travelled Teyvat with Dainsleif, then learned the "truth of this world", parted ways with him and joined the Order. Chlothar vanished and was presumed dead in Avidya Forest, and the sibling came to lead it.

Nod krai and snezhnaya revelations: From Version 6.0 the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter showed Rerir's history: he was an intelligence officer and Tholindis' fiancé, left Khaenri'ah to follow her through a moon gate, and survived as fragments that became the Wild Hunt monsters of Nod-Krai. Dottore revived him; Columbina, empowered with his own siphoned power, flung him through a gate beyond the sky that Dainsleif held open and then closed, sealing him away.

14.content: Khaenri'ah was founded about 6,000 years ago, around the time of Sal Vindagnyr's fall, as a nation without gods. It lay underground beneath what is now the Sumeru desert; its founders once lived aboveground.

15.content: The Crimson Moon Dynasty was Khaenri'ah's first known ruling house, associated with worship of the Crimson Moon. Its descendants carry the Balemoon Bloodfire. The legend of Perinheri is set in this period. The dynasty fell in a coup and the Eclipse Dynasty took over; Irmin later hunted its descendants.

16.content: The Eclipse Dynasty ruled from about the Archon War to the Cataclysm, embracing machines and "secrets from beyond the skies". Its last ruler was Irmin, the final Vinster King. Dainsleif and Halfdan served in its royal guard, the Black Serpent Knights.

17.content: Irmin named the Traveler's sibling heir and "Savior", then used them as a vessel to absorb unlimited Abyssal power. When Vedrfolnir warned against it, Irmin blinded and jailed him. The palace raid that followed produced the Five Sinners.

18.content: Dainsleif organised a raid with Rerir, Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir and Surtalogi to free his brother Vedrfolnir. The Abyssal power in the sibling, left unguarded amid the monsters Irmin's mechanisms attracted, led the Sinners to take a sixth each. None of them defended the kingdom later.

19.content: Anfortas, Marshal Regent, led the Schwanenritter and their Ruin Golems in evacuating Khaenri'ahns to Sumeru and fighting the Abyss. They were later honoured as the heroes of Dahri by Nagarjuna's Darshan. Anfortas' fate is unknown.

20.content: During the Cataclysm Ronova cursed pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns with immortality. They no longer die or age but still erode in body and mind.

21.content: According to the wiki, Khaenri'ahns descend from Anastasya (the Tsaritsa) and Saarelainen, who arrived from the sea of stars; their son had four-pointed star pupils. Khaenri'ahns honour her as the "Mother of Khaenri'ah".

22.content: Rerir, one of the Five Sinners, tried to follow his fiancée Tholindis through a moon gate; his body was scattered across Nod-Krai and became the Wild Hunt. He was later revived and cast out of Teyvat in Song of the Welkin Moon.

23.content:
Liyue/History (also: History of Liyue, Liyue history, Liyue timeline): Liyue's recorded past, in order. Lang-Gan on the western coast was destroyed by a Celestial Nail about 6,000 years ago and its survivors went to Chenyu Vale. Morax and the Goddess of Dust Guizhong then founded the Guili Assembly, which was ruined in an Archon War battle about 3,700 years ago. Morax led the survivors south of Mt. Tianheng to found Liyue Harbor, waged war on rival gods, and became the Geo Archon more than 2,000 years ago. Adepti and Yakshas guarded the land, the Cataclysm sent monsters out of the Chasm about 500 years ago, and the Liyue Qixing now govern in public. Most dates are approximate.

Use this entry for "what came before what" in Liyue. Fine detail on the Archon War, Cataclysm and the Unified Civilization belongs to their own entries, and the individual places and people have their own entries.

Lang gan and chenyu vale: The wiki places the civilisation of Lang-Gan in what is now the Chasm, part of the unified civilisation of Teyvat, with the angel Zibai as Celestia's divine envoy. About 6,000 years ago, while Morax was still young, the Heavenly Principles sent a Celestial Nail down on Lang-Gan to cleanse Abyssal corruption. Zibai held the Nail back for a time so that the people could flee, and died doing so. Lang-Gan was destroyed, the impact created the Chasm, and the Nail's remains lie deep beneath it as the Spiritstone. The survivors settled in Chenyu Vale.

Guili assembly: In a period of peace before the Archon War, Morax descended on the land, raised Mt. Tianheng, calmed the seas and defeated sea monsters such as Baqiu. Guizhong, the Lord of Dust, befriended him, and together they founded the Guili Assembly between Mt. Tianheng and the Stone Gate. Its name takes the first character of Guizhong's name and one character of the name Morax then used (the name itself is unknown). It prospered through farming, mining and trade. Guizhong set four commandments for her people, about unity, wisdom, a supple body and growing virtue. She and the Cloud Retainer, among other adepti, built the Guizhong Ballistas to defend it. The wiki says the sources disagree about which god came first.

Archon war morax: After the Guili Assembly fell, Liyue Harbor was founded about 3,700 years ago. Morax created the Millelith to guard the people against monsters, taught people to build houses using Mora as a model, set minted Mora as the currency and made a contract with the adepti to defend the harbor. He then decided to make war on the other gods, as the only way to restore order and protect humanity. The adepti and Yakshas fought for him. Over the next centuries, by the wiki's tentative ordering, he beat many gods and sea monsters. He became the Geo Archon, ending the war in Liyue, more than 2,000 years ago.

24.content: The Guili Assembly was an ancient Liyue civilisation founded by Morax and the Lord of Dust Guizhong between Mt. Tianheng and the Stone Gate. It was prosperous, a trading hub with strong engineering, and was protected by the adepti and the Guizhong Ballistas. A battle of the Archon War about 3,700 years ago destroyed it and killed Guizhong; the survivors went south to found Liyue Harbor.

25.content: Lang-Gan was an ancient civilisation on the western coast of Liyue, in the area that became the Chasm, governed by the angel Zibai. A Celestial Nail destroyed it about 6,000 years ago; Zibai died holding it back so her people could flee. Survivors went to Chenyu Vale.

26.content: Havria was a gentle, militarily weak god of salt who lost her lands in the Archon War until only Sal Terrae remained. Her followers ended her life painlessly, and the power released turned the city to salt. Yinyuan Hall's descendants now misremember her as killed by Morax.

27.content: A Liyue legend of a Sea God who traded a year without storms for a human bride. After a bride asked for his help when her daughter was to be taken, he destroyed her village. Whether he existed, or relates to the ruins at Qingxu Pool, is unknown.

28.content: Yakshas were adepti summoned by Morax to suppress the lingering hatred of defeated gods. The five strongest were Bosacius, Bonanus, Menogias, Indarias and Alatus (Xiao). Karma, madness and the Cataclysm left Xiao the only known Yaksha.

29.content: The Geo dragon Azhdaha, once blind and healed by Morax, lost his memory and, about 1,000 years ago, rampaged after mining disturbed the ley lines. Morax and the adepti sealed him in a pocket dimension at Nantianmen.

30.content: In the Cataclysm a meteorite struck the Chasm and monsters poured out. Bosacius, the thaumaturge Boyang and the Millelith vanguard used the Fantastic Compass to seal the beasts at the cost of their lives.

31.content: The Rite of Homa began as cremation to stop a karmic plague spread by the corpses of slain gods. Its pioneers founded Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, whose family motto is that only an unbound flame can purify the world.

32.content:
Timeline of Teyvat (also: Master Timeline, Teyvat Timeline, Teyvat Chronology, History of Teyvat): Teyvat's recorded past runs in ordered eras. Before the Heavenly Principles came, dragons led by the Seven Sovereigns held the world. The Heavenly Principles and their four Shades defeated them and made a world for humanity. Around 6,000 years ago a second war ended with the Celestial Nails cast down to purge Abyssal corruption. Gods then fought over seven divine seats in the Archon War (6,000 to 2,000 years ago), which ended with the first Seven. About 500 years ago the Cataclysm destroyed Khaenri'ah and let the Abyss spill across the world. The Traveler's story begins after that: the twins fall into Teyvat, one is sealed for 500 years, and the Archon Quests follow the search region by region up to Snezhnaya in Version 7.1. Dates before the Archon War are approximate and partly reconstructed by editors.

Use this entry for "what came before what" and for rough "how long ago". For depth on any era or nation, defer to the regional history entries and the lore entries for the Archon War, the Cataclysm and the fall of Khaenri'ah. Order of eras: Old World, When the Doves Held Branches, Unified Civilization, War of Funerary Flame, Interim Period, Archon War, Post-Archon War, Pre-Cataclysm, Cataclysm, Post-Cataclysm, Recent Past, then the story-present.

Eras overview: Old World; When the Doves Held Branches; Unified Civilization; War of Funerary Flame (about 6,000 years ago); Interim Period; Archon War (6,000 to 2,000 years ago); Post-Archon War (2,000 to 500 years ago); Pre-Cataclysm; Cataclysm (500 years ago); Post-Cataclysm (500 to 100 years ago); Recent Past (under 100 years ago); the present (the Archon Quests).

Round figures the wiki gives: the Archon War runs "6000 to 2000 years ago"; the Post-Archon War period runs 2,000 to 500 years ago, across which the original Cryo, Dendro, Electro, Hydro and Pyro Archons gradually died out; the Cataclysm is 500 years ago; the Post-Cataclysm period is 500 to 100 years ago; the Recent Past is less than 100 years ago. Mondstadt's own refounding by Barbatos is placed about 2,600 years ago in this archive's Mondstadt entry. Spans overlap: the end of the War of Funerary Flame blends into the start of the Archon War, and the wiki's Archon War section itself includes events after the Celestial Nails fell.

Cataclysm: The Cataclysm began when the Abyss invaded the surface world and devastated much of Teyvat. Teyvat's people blame one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, "Gold" Rhinedottir, whose Alfisol were the monsters' vanguard. The Kingdom of Khaenri'ah was destroyed by the Heavenly Principles, ending the Eclipse Dynasty and its civilisation and sending ripples across the world; the Seven became involved after the Abyss invaded. Natlan suffered more than any other region because its ley lines were weakened, and the Night Warden Wars began there. Hilichurl numbers rose sharply as Khaenri'ahns of foreign ancestry were turned into hilichurls as punishment, while pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns were cursed with immortality and slow erosion.

Story present: The Traveler arrives in Teyvat in Mondstadt and follows the Archon Quests: Prologue (Mondstadt), Chapter I (Liyue), Chapter II (Inazuma), Chapter III (Sumeru), Chapter IV (Fontaine), Chapter V (Natlan), the Song of the Welkin Moon arc (Nod-Krai) and Chapter VII (Snezhnaya, Versions 7.0 and 7.1).

Connections: Cross-reference the regional history entries (Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru, Fontaine, Natlan, Snezhnaya, Khaenri'ah), the Archon War and Cataclysm lore entries, the Unified Civilization and War of Funerary Flame entries, and the Night Warden Wars. Cosmology entries for the Seven Sovereigns, Heavenly Principles, Four Shades, Celestia, Three Moons, False Sky and Celestial Nails give background; the Fatui and the Abyss Order drive the story-present.

Status as of 7.1: Current to Version 7.1 (2026-09-23): the Traveler is in Snezhnaya after Ronova's fall, and the fallen Celestial Nails have begun emitting pillars of light. Pre-Archon-War dating stays approximate.

33.comment: Timeline of Teyvat: Archon War dating
33.content: The Archon War ran from about 6,000 to 2,000 years ago, when seven divine seats opened and gods fought over them, ending when the last seat was claimed. See the dedicated Archon War entry for the war itself; here it is a marker between the War of Funerary Flame and the Post-Archon War.

34.content: The Cataclysm happened about 500 years ago: Khaenri'ah was destroyed by the Heavenly Principles and the Abyss invaded the surface world. Asmoday sealed both twins around this time, and the Traveler slept for 500 years. See the Cataclysm and fall of Khaenri'ah lore entries for the event.

35.comment: Timeline of Teyvat: War of Funerary Flame dating
35.content: Around 6,000 years ago the Heavenly Principles won the war against Nibelung's Abyssal rebellion and cast the Celestial Nails to purify Teyvat. Knowledge of the era before this war was forbidden. See the War of Funerary Flame entry for details.

36.comment: Timeline of Teyvat: The Wanderer's Trail
36.content: The Prologue's Wanderer's Trail shows the twins trying to leave Teyvat during the Cataclysm and being stopped by an unknown god (later shown to be Asmoday), who seals the Traveler and takes the sibling; the Traveler wakes 500 years later. Later quests show the twins had crash-landed on Teyvat earlier, before the Cataclysm. This anchors the story-present at roughly 500 years after the Cataclysm.

37.content:
Mondstadt/History (also: History of Mondstadt, Mondstadt Timeline, Mondstadt Chronology): Mondstadt's history runs from the lost northern kingdom of Arcadia and the snow-buried mountain city of Sal Vindagnyr, through the tyrant god Decarabian's walled city, which fell about 2,600 years ago when his people rebelled and the wind spirit Barbatos became the Anemo Archon. The noble clans who followed turned tyrannical until the gladiator Vennessa, about 1,000 years ago, overthrew them and founded the Knights of Favonius. About 500 years ago the Cataclysm brought the dragon Durin down on Mondstadt before Barbatos and Dvalin killed him. The recent past (to 7.1) covers the Ragnvindr family tragedy, the Stormterror crisis and Varka's expedition to Nod-Krai.

The sections below follow the order the wiki timeline uses: Unified Civilization, War of Funerary Flame, the Interim Period, the Archon War and Age of Kings, the aristocratic period, Mondstadt Reborn, the Cataclysm, the post-Cataclysm centuries, and the recent past. Many dates are only "unknown years ago", and the ordering is partly an editors' reconstruction.

Decarabians fall: About 2,600 years ago the people rose, led by the Nameless Bard, the wind spirit Barbatos, Decarabian's former lover Amos, Gunnhildr and the Red-Haired Warrior, with Gunnhildr's clan fighting too. Decarabian and Amos died, and his death unleashed a violent tempest.

Mondstadt reborn: About 1,000 years ago, after Ludi Harpastum, the cries of the oppressed woke Barbatos, who came down as the bard Venti and befriended Vennessa after she angered Barca Lawrence, heir of the Lawrence Clan. She was sentenced to gladiator matches for her people's freedom, the last against Ursa the Drake itself, which Lord Lawrence had bartered with to buy peace.

Cataclysm: About 500 years ago Arundolyn, Grand Master and the "Lion of Light", and his friend Rostam, the "Wolf Pup", led the Knights to fight monsters in Khaenri'ah during the Cataclysm; Rostam died there, and Arundolyn gave up fighting.

38.comment: Mondstadt/History: Arcadia and Sal Vindagnyr Timeline
38.content: Arcadia was the oak-forest civilisation of old Mondstadt, with Elysium in Windrest Peak under the Gunnhildr Clan. About 6,000 years ago an unknown calamity buried it in winter; Gunnhildr, the Knight of the Golden Bough, failed to find a living branch of Irminsul and led survivors south to shelter under Decarabian. On Vindagnyr (Dragonspine) the city of Sal Vindagnyr died beneath snow after the Skyfrost Nail fell, while the outlander Imunlaukr was away seeking Irminsul.

39.content: About 2,600 years ago, with Boreas' blizzards beating on his walls, Decarabian's people rose in rebellion under the code word Windblume. Decarabian and Amos died; the Nameless Bard's last song turned the tempest into Mondstadt's wind but cost the bard his life. The wind spirit became the Anemo Archon and kept the bard's name, Venti, then built the new city on Cider Lake and later withdrew.

40.content: About 1,000 years ago the gladiator Vennessa, a Muratan enslaved by the aristocrats, fought Ursa the Drake with Barbatos' help; the nobles were exiled and she founded the Knights of Favonius and restored the Church. A longer rebellion also involved a forged treaty selling Mondstadt to Morax.

41.comment: Mondstadt/History: The Cataclysm in Mondstadt Timeline
41.content: About 500 years ago Rostam died in Khaenri'ah, Arundolyn stopped fighting, and the dragon Durin devastated Mondstadt until Barbatos and Dvalin killed him on Dragonspine. Rostam's lover became the Crimson Witch of Flames and later Signora.

42.content:
Natlan/History (also: History of Natlan, Natlan timeline, Natlan history): Natlan's history in order: a dragon civilisation (Natlantea) under the Pyro Dragon Sovereign Xiuhcoatl; its fall about 2,000 years ago to Xbalanque, the first mortal Pyro Archon; the Eternal Empire of the half-dragon tyrant Och-Kan and his overthrow; and the Cataclysm 500 years ago, when the Abyss invaded and the Night Warden Wars began. They ended in Version 5.3 when the Traveler and Mavuika purged the Night Kingdom and Capitano gave his life.

Natlan never joined the Archon War; dragon infighting filled that age. Its distinct feature is a throne won by mortals: Pyro Archons are humans who prove themselves in battle. Use this entry for sequence and cause; use the linked entries for people, tribes and places.

Old world: Xiuhcoatl was born from the primal flame as the Pyro Dragon Sovereign and, the same day, split off a portion of that flame to create his younger brother Kukulkan. He hollowed out a space inside the Great Volcano of Tollan, founding the Sacred City of Tollan, and made the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, artificial intelligences, to govern Natlantea. The Legendary Tonatiuh was built to anchor a "cable" at Chichen Uctokah that leads beyond Teyvat's sky.

Ancient dragon era: From roughly 6,000 to 2,000 years ago the dragons of Natlantea ruled and humans were subordinate. Natlan took no part in the Archon War, because in-fighting among dragons absorbed everything; as a result its modern people know little about that war. Natlantea slowly declined and Kukulkan foresaw its end. He gave Phlogiston to the "primitive" humans and fathered Och-Kan, half dragon and half human, to unite the two peoples and rise to a new throne. Near the end of this age the tribes were founded, worshipping the Wayob (ancestors) and the Night Kingdom.

Xbalanque and the first pyro archon: About 2,000 years ago Xbalanque and his army invaded the Sacred City of Tollan. He killed Xiuhcoatl and became the first Pyro Archon of Natlan, ending the civilisation of Natlantea. The Three Princes and ten of the Thirteen Lords died in the fighting.

Ochkanatlan and och kan: About 2,000 years ago followers of Xbalanque founded Ochkanatlan, the Eternal Empire. After Xbalanque entered the Sacred Flame, Och-Kan became king. The seven tribes formed the Grand Alliance and put their authority in his hands. Och-Kan betrayed Xbalanque's commandments and became a tyrant: he sought to wipe out the dragons and their descendants, the Saurians, mistreated his people and banned ancestor worship and the Night Kingdom.

Cataclysm and night warden wars: Five hundred years ago the Abyss invaded, and Natlan, with weakened ley lines, suffered more than any other region. This began the Night Warden Wars. Great infighting among the tribes occurred as well. Bakunawa, a creature made by Rhinedottir, entered Tenochtzitoc and killed almost all the Muratans there except Tenoch, who had been exiled before the disaster. Several Pyro Archons (Cochanina, Shulevitz, Gloharry and Isaja) worked together to contain it; the first three died doing so and Isaja contained it.

Mavuikas plan: Mavuika's plan was that the tribes would spend 500 years regaining their strength, after which the Wayob would choose six new heroes to drive the Abyss out for good. She sacrificed her life to the Sacred Flame so that she could reawaken 500 years later to oversee it. Because of long exposure to the Abyss, Natlanese people had to remain within their borders, where the Wayob could protect them.

Present day 5 0 to 5 3: In Version 5.0 a Pilgrimage was held and Kachina beat Mualani in the finals; she, Chasca, Iansan and others fought in a Night Warden War, but the Ode of Resurrection did not revive Kachina when she fell. Mavuika suspended the Pilgrimage and the wars. With Vichama's help Kachina's Ancient Name was recovered, and the Traveler, Chasca, Iansan and Mualani entered the Night Kingdom and rescued her, then were trapped until Mavuika freed them by giving up keepsakes people had offered her in exchange for Contending Fire. Mualani was acknowledged by her Ancient Name, leaving only the Flower-Feather Clan and the Masters of the Night-Wind without heroes.

End of the war: In 5.3 Xilonen forged the Traveler an Ancient Name, and the Traveler and Mavuika entered the corroded Night Kingdom to purge Gosoythoth's influence. With Yohualtecuhtin's blessing the Traveler gained Pyro power. Gosoythoth became the Lord of Eroded Primal Fire and seemed to win, but the support of the Natlanese restored the Traveler and Mavuika, and they defeated it, ending the Night Warden Wars.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 the Abyss war is over; Mavuika survived its end, while Capitano gave his life and merged with the Lord of the Night, his body left on the Throne of the Primal Fire. The wiki's Natlan history records no later events.

Open questions: How the seven ancient tribes became six, who all the Pyro Archons were and when they ruled, and the precise dating of events before the Cataclysm are not settled by canon (see uncertainties).

43.comment: Natlan/History: Ochkanatlan Adventure Team and Bona
43.content: The Ochkanatlan Adventure Team under Taika went to the ruins of Ochkanatlan about 490 years ago seeking the Legendary Tonatiuh, hoping it would help against the Abyss. Kukulkan had laid a trap and took nearly everyone's souls. Taika's daughter Bona later found Och-Kan's mind in the Core of Chu'ulel, named it Cocouik and travelled with it to the Tonatiuh, where she died too.

44.comment: Natlan/History: Tenoch and the Heroes of Natlan
44.content: Tenoch was an exile from Tenochtzitoc who survived Bakunawa. He gathered fighters from the six tribes to defend Natlan from the Abyss; they are the Heroes of Natlan, and Mavuika joined them as a new Pyro Archon. The Mare Jivari is the site of their battle.

45.comment: Natlan/History: Pyro Archons Who Contained Bakunawa
45.content: When Bakunawa destroyed Tenochtzitoc, four Pyro Archons (Cochanina, Shulevitz, Gloharry and Isaja) united to restrain it. Three died in the effort; Isaja held it. Pyro Archons are mortal, so their deaths pass the title on.

46.content: The Night Warden Wars were the long war against the Abyss in the Night Kingdom, beginning with the Cataclysm 500 years ago. The Pilgrimage selected warriors to fight them, and the Ode of Resurrection revived the fallen. They ended in Version 5.3.

47.content:
Snezhnaya/History (also: History of Snezhnaya, Snezhnayan history, Nod-Krai history, History of Nod-Krai): Snezhnaya's history runs from the golden city of Hyperborea (destroyed by a Celestial Nail about 6,000 years ago) through the Pale Star Court of the Belyi Tsar, first Cryo Archon, who ruled until he fell fighting the Abyss in the Cataclysm 500 years ago. Anastasya then became Tsaritsa, broke the fae aristocracy, founded the Fatui with Pierro, and let Nod-Krai become an autonomous land guarded by the Lightkeepers. As of 7.1 she holds six Gnoses and is waging a hidden war on Celestia.

Use this entry for "what came before what" in Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai. Order: Hyperborea and the first fae; the Pale Star Court (Kitezh, Belyi Tsar); the Abyssal gate and Anastasya's erasure and return; the Belyi Tsar as Cryo Archon and the pioneering age of Nod-Krai; the Cataclysm; the Tsaritsa's accession and reforms; the Fatui and Harbingers; Nod-Krai in the Song of the Welkin Moon; and 7.0-7.1. Absolute dates are mostly round figures from item texts and are partly wiki reconstruction.

Hyperborea: Over 6,000 years ago, in the Unified Civilization era, the Golden City of Hyperborea stood in ancient Snezhnaya, then a warm, green land. It drew on the power of the Three Moons. According to artifact texts, its people angered the angels by questioning the progress of knowledge; the voyager Anacharsis, living in the guise of a Hyperborean boy, was sent before the first angel Koitar, and the two became lovers who resolved to oppose the Heavenly Principles. Hyperborean artisans made the Snowland Fae using forbidden methods Koitar taught.

Saarelainen and anastasya: Over 6,000 years ago the Third Descender Saarelainen came from the sea of stars to ancient Snezhnaya and entered a relationship with Anastasya; they had a son, and their descendants became the Khaenri'ahns. Thousands of years later, as a herald of the Belyi Tsar's Pale Star Court, Anastasya and Saarelainen were incited by the Tsar to open a gate to the Abyss (the Hymns of the Far North place it on Pohjola). The Abyss began seeping into the world and the Heavenly Principles erased Anastasya.

Pale star court: The Belyi Tsar (Monomakh Snezhnyi) is said to have emerged around 5,000 years ago from the Cryo Dragon's remains and to have believed himself a fae. He founded Kitezh, the first city of Snezhnaya and capital of the Pale Star Court, and about 3,000 years ago won the war against King Miscislav of the Volkodlak Alliance by killing him and two fae Grand Dukes with a thrown spear. All fae clans then swore fealty and he took the title Belyi Tsar. Snezhnaya was an imperial aristocracy led by the Snowland Fae, living in luxury.

Cataclysm in the north: In the Cataclysm 500 years ago, Nod-Krai was the first land corrupted by the Abyss, which appeared as the Wild Hunt. Neither the royal court nor any god defended it, and Abyssal monsters razed it. The Belyi Tsar fell in a battle against the Abyss during his expedition. Solovei, called the first Torchforger, and Aila, the Scions' first Moonchanter, turned the tide with the moons' power, and Solovei and his allies founded the Lightkeepers, swearing to defend Nod-Krai.

Tsaritsas accession: Anastasya succeeded the Belyi Tsar during the Cataclysm and was crowned Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya. Some fae nobles, furious a non-fae ruled, refused to recognise her; the Dalegrad clan broke ties with Snezhnograd and Flins left in self-imposed exile. She was left bitter and cut ties with other Archons, including Barbatos (reason unclear). She approved Solovei's request to make Nod-Krai an autonomous region under the Lightkeepers by Edict.

48.content: Hyperborea was the golden civilization of ancient Snezhnaya, over 6,000 years ago, that powered its magic with the Three Moons' tides. It created the Snowland Fae with Koitar's forbidden methods, and was destroyed by a Celestial Nail. Survivors fled to Hiisi Island and became the Frostmoon Scions.

49.comment: Snezhnaya/History: Pale Star Court and Kitezh
49.content: The Pale Star Court was the fae empire of the Belyi Tsar (Monomakh Snezhnyi), centred on Kitezh, the first city of Snezhnaya. Kitezhgrad was later destroyed by the Abyss and the survivors founded Novokitezhgrad. After the Tsar became Cryo Archon, the court moved to Snezhnograd and the nation was renamed Snezhnaya.

50.content: The Belyi Tsar's exploration and industrial development of Nod-Krai over 500 years ago. The Khaenri'ahn exile Rauthvangi came to court as "Rotwang" and encouraged the Tsar's rebellion against the Heavenly Principles.

51.content: After the Cataclysm Solovei, the first Torchforger, and Aila used the moons' power against the Wild Hunt, and Solovei founded the Lightkeepers. The Tsaritsa's Edict approved their jurisdiction and Nod-Krai's autonomy. Aila gave Solovei the Arrow of Terpikeraunas. Their insignia is a nightingale holding a burning wick; headquarters are at Piramida.

52.comment: Snezhnaya/History: Reed Miller and the Treasure Hoarders
52.content: Reed Miller, born Avrelian to a Frostmoon maiden and a Snezhnayan officer, became an infamous thief across Teyvat who dreamed of an Elysium for the poor and founded the Treasure Hoarders. The royal court sentenced him to death; whether he died is disputed between item texts.

53.comment: Snezhnaya/History: Tsaritsa's Accession and the Fae Princes
53.content: Early in her reign Anastasya crushed fae opposition: the Port Belovodye rebellion, the seizure of Drevogorye's lands, the Veche replacing fae rule, and the Imperial Order Reformation Edict of her seventh year, after which many princes renounced their titles. Many settled in Novokitezhgrad.

54.content: The Fatui were founded about 500 years ago by the Tsaritsa with Pierro, who served as its first member and Director. Their first campaign retook Port Belovodye. Individual Harbingers are covered in their own entries.

55.content: The Tsaritsa's highest-priority Edict, issued when Columbina left the Fatui, ordering her recovery at all costs. It was rescinded after Dottore's rogue conduct was dealt with.

56.content: In 7.1 the Tsaritsa slowed time with six Gnoses so Rhinedottir could not finish reviving Ronova's victims before Celestia's monitoring cycle; Celestia stripped Ronova of her authority and Pierro mortally wounded her with the Eye of the Fatui.

57.content:
Sumeru/History (also: History of Sumeru, Sumeru timeline, Sumeru chronology): Sumeru's past runs from the dragon Apep's forest and the first Celestial Nail's burying of it, through the three God-Kings (Nabu Malikata, King Deshret and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata), Deshret's fall to forbidden knowledge and the desert's age of city-states, to the cataclysm 500 years ago, when Rukkhadevata was replaced by Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida) and the sages came to rule in her name. Chapter III (3.0-3.2) freed Nahida; in 6.6 she burned Irminsul to end Dottore's attack, and Aaru took over its work.

Use this entry for the order of events and rough "how long ago". Canon seldom gives years for pre-cataclysm Sumeru. The rainforest and the desert have separate histories (Rukkhadevata's and Deshret's) that were later tangled and distorted by the Akademiya's misinformation.

Old world to war: In the Old World the Dendro Dragon Sovereign Apep ruled the land that became Sumeru and nursed ancient Dendro lifeforms. Irminsul first grew there as a fern in her court. The Heavenly Principles took Apep's Dendro Authority and remade Irminsul into the device that records Teyvat's information and keeps the cycle of erosion running. In the Unified Civilization the ancient city of Ys stood in what is now the Sumeru desert, and Rukkhadevata, Irminsul's avatar, already existed.

Three god kings: During the Archon War Nabu Malikata, a surviving Angel later called the Goddess of Flowers, befriended King Deshret and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. The three became known as the Three Eternal Companion-Gods of Sumeru and each held a share of the realm: the banquet, authority and life. Nabu Malikata and Deshret built Ay-Khanoum, the City of Amphitheaters, whose name means "City of the Moon Maiden" in the Jinn tongue. Deshret defeated many gods, among them Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth, who entered his service as the Seven Pillars; gods who refused, such as Remus, went wandering.

Deshret and gurabad: Deshret ruled the desert alone after Nabu Malikata's death, having made a deal with Apep that it would consume him after his death to take his knowledge. He chose vassal kings and priests, with the Jinn as messengers. The shepherd Ormazd founded Gurabad with help from the Jinni Liloupar, whom he married. Liloupar felt betrayed by his later tyranny and spent generations arranging the city's ruin. The folk book The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin blames Shirin and Shiruyeh; Liloupar's memories show otherwise. Deshret was furious on learning of it and split her soul into seven pieces, each guarded by a sage.

Fall of deshret: Deshret's research released forbidden knowledge. People heard whispers, dark scales (Eleazar) spread over them and the land withered. He asked Rukkhadevata for help. She came back to the desert, had priests build temples she filled with the power of life, and created the Akasha System to unite people's wisdom against the poison. The priest Kasala's record says the embers of Deshret's civilisation were preserved in Aaru Village, though other in-game accounts place the village's founding centuries later under the Old Blind Poet. This exhausted her and shrank her to a child's form. It was not enough, and Deshret sacrificed himself to end it. His civilisation broke into short-lived city-states.

Pre cataclysm: Slightly more than 500 years ago, Rosalyne-Kruzchka Lohefalter (later the Fatui Harbinger Signora) came from Mondstadt to study at the Sumeru Akademiya.

Cataclysm in sumeru: Five hundred years ago Rukkhadevata was not summoned to Khaenri'ah like the other Archons, because she was to protect Irminsul. Forbidden knowledge contaminated Irminsul and, since she was its avatar, her too. She used the Akasha System to borrow her people's wisdom and purge it, but could not erase herself, so she created Lesser Lord Kusanali from the purest branch of Irminsul to be her successor. She then left on a final journey and never returned. The forest's king Viaghara died defending the forest.

Post cataclysm: After the cataclysm Lesser Lord Kusanali was found and brought to Sumeru City. The people rejoiced and the Sabzeruz Festival moved to her birthday. The sages found her no wiser than an ordinary child and shut her in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, while espousing Rukkhadevata's legacy and building the Akasha into a public information network. Over 400 years ago the student Zandik, who became the Fatui Harbinger Dottore, studied at the Akademiya, and the Temple of Silence left the corrupt sages for a temple at Thamud Oasis.

Present day: In Chapter III (3.0 to 3.2) the sages' plan to build an artificial god with Dottore and the Fatui was defeated, Nahida was freed, the Akasha shut down, and Nahida purged Rukkhadevata from Irminsul, removing the forbidden knowledge and ending Eleazar. In Khvarena of Good and Evil the ex-Skeptic Klingsor tried with Nasejuna to break the Harvisptokhm's seal, and the Traveler and the Pari Sorush stopped them. In 6.6 Dottore attacked Irminsul from within and Sumeru City was evacuated; Nahida burned the tree with the Pyro Gnosis and Aaru, reprogrammed by Alhaitham and Kaveh, took over its role.

58.comment: Sumeru/History: The Three God-Kings and Ay-Khanoum
58.content: Nabu Malikata, King Deshret and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata ruled Sumeru together for a time and built Ay-Khanoum as an earthly paradise. Each valued a different kind of wisdom and they debated often. The partnership broke over Deshret's quest for forbidden knowledge. Ay-Khanoum was later abandoned and then rebuilt among the seven cities of the post-Deshret era.

59.content: Gurabad was a vassal state of Deshret founded by the shepherd Ormazd with the Jinni Liloupar. Liloupar, seeing her husband become a tyrant, planned its destruction and used her children and grandson. The in-world book blames Shirin; Liloupar's own memories show she was the planner. Deshret punished her by splitting her soul into seven parts.

60.content: The rainforest was created by Rukkhadevata after she left the desert. The Varuna Contraption terraforms the land, the Wall of Samiel stops desertification, and the Aranara and the forest lords guard it. Viaghara, the first lord of the forest, died defending the forest in the cataclysm, and the Rishboland Tigers are his successors.

61.content: In 6.6 Dottore corrupted Irminsul from within. Sumeru City was evacuated. Nahida, invoking her authority as keeper of Irminsul before the three Shades, burned it with the Pyro Gnosis that Mavuika had given the Traveler, and Dottore died in the fire, which burned for seven days and nights. Aaru, modified under Alhaitham and Kaveh's plan with help from the freed Pillars Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf, now holds the world's records. The Pyro Gnosis is gone.

62.content:
Archon War (also: Archon Wars, War of the Archons, era of warring gods): The Archon War (Chinese and Japanese: War of the Demon Gods) was the long age of fighting between gods that followed the war of funerary flame about 6,000 years ago and ended about 2,000 years ago. The Heavenly Principles set up seven divine thrones in Celestia, one per element, and let the gods fight over them and their Gnoses. The victors became The Seven, the Archons who founded and shaped the seven nations. Of the original victors, only Barbatos (Venti) and Morax (Zhongli) remain as of 7.1; the other five seats have changed hands.

The war was not one conflict but many regional struggles that ended at different times. Mondstadt's was settled 2,600 years ago when Decarabian fell; Morax was already fighting for Liyue before 3,700 years ago; the era as a whole closed about 2,000 years ago, when the last seat was claimed. Natlan was never part of it. Most defeated gods who survived fled beyond Teyvat into the Dark Sea.

Established: - After the war of funerary flame, the Heavenly Principles (the "usurper" of Neuvillette's Vision story) were too badly wounded to suppress the world's original order directly. They dismantled the unified civilization, banned its history and decided on a "new order".
- The angels who had guided humanity were cursed and cast out of Celestia, and a new class of gods emerged to take that role.
- Seven divine thrones were set up in Celestia, each holding part of an elemental Authority taken from the Seven Sovereigns. Gods fought for them and the matching Gnoses.
- Ningguang tells the Traveler that many gods walked the earth and fought long wars that did not abate until 2,000 years ago, with much blood shed.
- Zhongli's character story: Rex Lapis remembers the moment the final Archon took their seat, ending the Archon War and the era of warring gods.

Theatres: - Mondstadt: Barbatos and the rebels overthrew Decarabian, God of Storms, 2,600 years ago; Boreas declined the throne.
- Liyue: Morax, after Guizhong's death, founded Liyue Harbor and sealed many gods (Osial, Chi, the mistress of Chenyu Vale); Havria and Marchosius fell or gave up their godhood.
- Inazuma: Makoto and Ei united the islands; Orobashi fled into Enkanomiya.
- Sumeru: King Deshret, Rukkhadevata and Nabu Malikata ruled together until Deshret's pursuit of forbidden knowledge; Rukkhadevata is presumed to have ascended afterwards.
- Fontaine: Remus' Remuria rose and sank; Celestia then made Egeria the Hydro Archon.
- Natlan: never part of the war; Xbalanque defeated the Pyro Sovereign and became the first Pyro Archon.
- Snezhnaya: Monomakh united the fae clans and became the Belyi Tsar.

Aftermath: The war closed about 2,000 years ago with the last seat claimed. Most defeated gods who survived refused the new order and fled to remote islands in the Dark Sea, where they became "evil gods"; Bit of Aerosiderite notes their power came from the same source as Rex Lapis'. Some gods instead cooperated with The Seven, such as Boreas (as one of the Four Winds) and Marchosius. The original Seven used to drink together in Liyue.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): to people in the present the Archon War is ancient history and legend, known through local tales, operas and ruins rather than memory. Only long-lived beings remember it: Zhongli, Venti, the adepti, Ei, Boreas and certain dragons. Its scars are physical: Guyun Stone Forest, Sal Terrae, the split Yashiori Island, Stormterror's Lair. Liyue's opera and storytellers favour the "Warrior God" Morax; Mondstadt tells its version as the tale of freedom won from a tyrant. In Natlan, people barely know of it.

63.content: 2,600 years ago Barbatos, a nameless bard, Amos, a red-haired warrior and Gunnhildr led Old Mondstadt's people against Decarabian. The god fell, his storm wall broke, the bard and Amos died, and Barbatos became the Anemo Archon. Boreas, who had besieged the city for ages, judged himself unfit for the throne.

64.comment: Archon War: Gods of Liyue in the Archon War
64.content: Morax fought alongside Guizhong and Marchosius before founding Liyue Harbor. He sealed Osial and other sea gods at Guyun Stone Forest, slew Chi at Qingce, defeated the mistress of Chenyu Vale and drove Orobashi to Inazuma. Havria was killed by her own king; Marchosius gave up his godhood to protect Liyue. Xiao is the last active Yaksha of those who cleared the dead gods' demons.

65.comment: Archon War: Orobashi and the Shogunate
65.content: Orobashi fled the war after losing to Morax and the Electro god, became Enkanomiya's god, later raised Watatsumi Island, and was killed by Ei in a later war over Yashiori Island; his resentment became the Tatarigami.

66.comment: Archon War: Gods who fled to the Dark Sea
66.content: Many defeated gods refused to live under The Seven and fled to remote islands of the Dark Sea, where coastal nations call them evil gods. Their powers came from the same source as Rex Lapis'. Enkanomiya was also counted as outside The Seven's domain.

67.content:
Asmoday's Defection (also: Asmoday defected, Asmoday's new master, Asmoday switched sides, Ruler of Space's absence, Asmoday's absence): Asmoday, the Ruler of Space and "Sustainer of the Heavenly Principles", once stopped the Traveler and their twin from leaving Teyvat and tore them apart. Five hundred years later she no longer attends the meetings of the four Shades and has left her own Temple of Space. Hints point to her now working with the Traveler's sibling. Canon does not say why, or on whose terms.

The word "defection" is the other Shades' interpretation, not a confession. Istaroth floats the idea that she "switched sides" and says looking for her would do more harm than good. Ronova calls such a move unthinkable unless Asmoday loved a new master more than herself. In 6.5 her abandoned attendant Melanta asks why she chose the sibling over him. In 7.1 a hooded figure is seen beside her.

Established: - In the prologue (1.0), a white-clad god calls herself the sustainer of the Heavenly Principles, says "the arrogation of mankind ends now", and traps both twins in swarms of red-black cubes. The Traveler's sibling is taken first; the Traveler is sealed and sleeps.
- Later canon names her Asmoday, Ruler of Space, one of the four Shades the Heavenly Principles created.

- In the Gods' Limits teaser (2025-07-09) Ronova, Rhinedottir and Istaroth meet in Celestia without Asmoday. Ronova notes that not one of the Shades has ever missed a meeting and wants her found.
- Asmoday's Temple of Space, the private domain where she kept chosen people and things from Teyvat, was left without its owner. Its rules began to fail; her attendant Nihilita walked away, and Melanta, the other attendant, tightened the rules until he began to destroy himself.
- In 6.5 (A Long Day in the Mountains, final chapter) Melanta asks his creator why she would choose the Traveler's sibling and abandon him. The portals she had opened nearby close as the fight ends.
- In 7.1 the Tsaritsa tells Rhinedottir she recently saw Asmoday with a hooded figure at the heart of a storm in Snezhnaya, near a monster that had come in with the snow. The hooded figure said it was worth witnessing the end of the Third Descender's story. Asmoday then used space to take them both away.

Accounts: - **Istaroth** (teaser): the meetings are only a formality, and Asmoday may simply have "switched sides". She adds that finding her would do more harm than good, then draws attention to Pierro's gaze when Ronova will not let the matter go.
- **Ronova** (teaser): wants her found, because no Shade has ever missed a meeting; says a change of side would be unthinkable unless she "loves her new master more than her own self".
- **Rhinedottir** (teaser; 7.1): finds the idea interesting. In 7.1 she asks whether the hooded figure is Asmoday's "new master". Naberius replies that this is more likely an idea Istaroth had on a whim.

Open questions: - Why did the Shade who sealed the twins end up apparently helping one of them?
- Who, if anyone, is her "new master", and did she choose to follow them?

- Did the sibling free her, persuade her, or was it her own decision?
- Do the Heavenly Principles know? They have been dormant, and Ronova names their waking as a condition for dealing with the Fatui.
- Why was she watching a storm monster in Snezhnaya, and why did a hooded figure speak of the end of the Third Descender's story?

Connections: Her story runs through the Traveler's sibling's thread (see lore.travelers-sibling-goals), the dormancy of the Heavenly Principles, the Third Descender's seal and the Temple of Space. Istaroth's unexplained choices in the same period are covered in lore.istaroths-intentions.

68.content: Asmoday, the Ruler of Space, once sealed the Traveler and their twin and now appears to be working with the twin. The other Shades suspect that she has defected, and Ronova suggests she might love a new master more than herself. In 6.5 her attendant Melanta asks why she chose the Traveler's sibling over him. No scene explains why. Do not name her master or her motive as fact.

69.content: In the interlude teaser The Gods' Limits (2025-07-09), the Shades meet in Celestia with Asmoday missing. Ronova insists she be found because no Shade has ever skipped a meeting. Istaroth wonders whether she simply "switched sides" and thinks finding her would do more harm than good. Ronova says the idea is unthinkable unless Asmoday loves a new master above herself. When she raises it again, Istaroth tells her Pierro is watching them. The scene gives no answer.

70.comment: Asmoday's Defection: Hooded Figure With Asmoday
70.content: In Black Feathers Scattered at Parting (7.1), Anastasya tells Rhinedottir she saw Asmoday with a hooded figure beside a storm monster. The figure said it was worth witnessing the end of the Third Descender's story. Asmoday used space and both vanished. Anastasya cannot say who the figure was; the quest stills and the wiki suggest it was the Traveler's sibling. Rhinedottir wonders whether it was Asmoday's "new master". Naberius dismisses the theory as one of Istaroth's passing ideas.

71.content: In the last chapter of A Long Day in the Mountains, Melanta defends the Temple of Space's rules after Asmoday's departure. Defeated, he asks why she chose the Traveler's sibling and abandoned him, admits he hoped for her praise, and ends in self-destruction. As he dies, Asmoday's portals nearby close, suggesting she may be watching. It is his own interpretation of her motives.

72.content:
Byakuyakoku (also: Tokoyokoku, Aphotic Earth, ancient Enkanomiya, Delphi Pytho, Land of Sun and Moon): Byakuyakoku, also called Tokoyokoku and originally Delphi Pytho, was an ancient human civilisation that belonged to the single world-spanning culture of the first era. In the war of funerary flame its land fell into the sea and was cut off from the surface. Its people, surrounded by darkness and by the vishaps called Dragonheirs of the Depths, built an artificial sun, the Dainichi Mikoshi, which gave them the cycle of Whitenight and Evernight. Later the fallen god Orobashi became their patron and led them back to the surface as the Watatsumi people. The place is now called Enkanomiya.

Its memory survives in a forbidden chronicle, Before Sun and Moon, in the five-volume Byakuyakoku Collection, and in the ruins beneath Watatsumi Island. Players meet it in the 2.4 Enkanomiya content.

Established: - Origin: before its fall, the people of Delphi Pytho were part of the unified civilisation that spanned the world. The chronicle describes the Heavenly Principles defeating the Seven Sovereigns and the creation of humanity under a covenant, and calls the supreme being "the Primordial One", with four shining Shades.
- Fall: in the Funerary Year the second throne of the heavens came, war was rekindled, and the chroniclers' ancestors and their land "fell into this place". The chronicle calls the second throne's coming only that; the wiki identifies it with the war of funerary flame, when Nibelung returned.
- Years of Darkness: in the depths they met the Dragonheirs of the Depths, who loved the dark and shunned light. Lanterns kept them back only partly, and the prayers of the people went unanswered by the Primordial One and three of its Shades.
- Istaroth: only the Ruler of Time, whom the chroniclers call Kairos or Tokoyo Ookami (and write backwards as "Htoratsi"), answered. In the Year of Blindness the sage Abrax (Aberaku in Narukami-style naming) woke to wisdom and led the building of Helios, the divine chariot of the sun, later the Dainichi Mikoshi.
- Years of Sun and Moon: when Helios was finished the Whitenight came and Evernight was banished. The people tried to find the way home but a ban from the first throne barred them. Abrax was imprisoned by order of the Sunchild, whom the people had chosen as king.
- Names: book 3 notes that its own title changed over the years from "Aphotic Earth" to "Tokoyokoku" and then "Byakuyakoku" (byakuya means white night); the wiki reads this as the land's successive names, and volume 1 does use Tokoyokoku for the land. After Watatsumi came, the land was renamed Enkanomiya and the surface home Sangonomiya.

Accounts: - The Byakuyakoku chronicle (Before Sun and Moon) is the voice of the old civilisation. It is pious toward the Primordial One and bitter about being abandoned. The wiki says Celestia wanted this history concealed, and Orobashi later banned the book as well.
- Watatsumi tradition (Sangonomiya Chronicles) tells the same history from the viewpoint of the people saved by Orobashi: a child asks a great serpent to be their god, the Sunchild's rule falls, and coral from the god's body makes the road to the surface.
- Present-day Watatsumi practice (the Goryou Matsuri quests) holds that every few thousand years Enkanomiya bleaches Watatsumi's soil and risks releasing the Dragonheirs, and the Goryou Matsuri ritual, using coral from the depths, is how the island guards against this. At the end of the limited-time 2.4 event Three Realms Gateway Offering, Kokomi resolves to find another method so the vishaps are no longer disturbed.
- Enjou of the Abyss Order claimed the book Before Sun and Moon would prove the gods came from outside Teyvat.

Open questions: - The surviving text does not say how many generations lived under the Sunchildren, nor how long passed between the fall and Orobashi's arrival.
- It is not stated what the "Second Who Came" is; the chroniclers only guess it was defeated.
- It is unknown why only Istaroth heard the people, or what she wanted from helping them.
- Whether the vishap-people exist is left open.

Connections: - Parent culture: the unified civilisation (Delphi Pytho is listed there as a member).
- Setting that survives it: Enkanomiya, the Dainichi Mikoshi, Watatsumi Island.
- Patron: Istaroth (as Tokoyo Ookami), then Orobashi (Watatsumi Omikami).
- Founding sage: Aberaku. Other figures: Antei (Antigonus in the old naming) and Spartacus (Supada). The Yuna Clan of Watatsumi, later home of the shrine maiden Mouun, is among the old houses that came up from Byakuyakoku.
- Opponent: the Bathysmal Vishaps; modern Abyss interest: Enjou.

73.content: The Sunchild was the king of Byakuyakoku. The book says the people chose him, crowned him and worshipped him, and that he ruled harshly and framed the righteous; the wiki, summarising quest text, says he was a child puppet of corrupt nobles who played on his fear of Aberaku. The line of Sunchildren ended when Orobashi came.

74.comment: Byakuyakoku: Helios, Hyperion and the Dainichi Mikoshi
74.content: The artificial sun of Byakuyakoku, built under Aberaku with knowledge from Istaroth. Its light drove back the Dragonheirs and brought Whitenight; its absence is Evernight. The wiki says Orobashi later strengthened it so day and night could be switched. Its names changed with the culture: Helios and Hyperion in the old tongue, Dainichi Mikoshi in the Watatsumi era.

75.content: The old name for the Bathysmal Vishaps that ruled the depths when the land fell. They loved the dark, were driven back by Helios, and were later sealed and studied under Orobashi. Book 5 notes that they had evolved to wield other elements, which is why the Dragon of Water was not expected to arise from them.

76.content: Whitenight is the lit state of the land, Evernight the dark state. Book 5 says the land's two odd phenomena, the mirages and the Sinshades, were at first both called Eidolons; only after Orobashi came were they told apart, and the mirages of Whitenight were named Sunfire Phantasms and those of Evernight Ghostfire Phantasms (later all called Sunfire Phantasms). In the 2.4 content, the spectral Sinshades (Shades of Tokoyo) appear during Evernight.

77.content: In Byakuyakoku, Istaroth was worshipped as Tokoyo Ookami, "the thousand winds", Kairos and God of Moments. Her power was named the undying wind and treated as one of the land's two great forces, the other being water. The chroniclers dared write her true name only once, reversed. Her wider story is in her own entry.

78.content:
Cataclysm (also: Dark Calamity, Calamity of Darkness, pitch-black calamity): The cataclysm was a disaster about five hundred years ago that struck all of Teyvat. Abyssal monsters poured out of Khaenri'ah, the underground kingdom that lived without gods, and ravaged every nation. The gods and the Heavenly Principles destroyed Khaenri'ah. Its people were cursed: pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns became immortal, and those of mixed blood became hilichurls and Abyss monsters. Several Archons died. Canon gives it no single proper name; people call it "the cataclysm", "the disaster" or "the Dark Calamity".

The cataclysm shaped the present world. The Traveler and their twin were separated by the god Asmoday as they tried to flee it. Three Archon seats changed hands: Inazuma (Makoto to Ei), Sumeru (Rukkhadevata to Nahida) and Fontaine (Egeria to Focalors). In Snezhnaya, the Belyi Tsar died and Anastasya, the Tsaritsa, took his place. Mavuika of Natlan sealed her own life in the Sacred Flame. The Abyss Order and the Fatui both arose in response to Celestia's actions. Since the cataclysm the Heavenly Principles have been asleep. Much about the disaster is still unresolved in canon, so do not fill the gaps with invention.

Established: Confirmed: about five hundred years ago, monsters carrying Abyssal power spread from Khaenri'ah across Teyvat. The gods and the Heavenly Principles struck Khaenri'ah and destroyed it; The Seven were summoned there. Ronova, the Ruler of Death, cursed its people. Most present-day people know little of it and treat much of it as legend.

- **Trigger:** King Irmin, the last Vinster King of the Eclipse Dynasty, named the Traveler's sibling his heir and "Savior". He then made them a vessel for unlimited Abyssal power. Five of his most esteemed subjects each took a sixth of that power and became the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah. None of them defended their homeland when the end came.
- **Who attacked:** all of The Seven were summoned to Khaenri'ah except Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who stayed to guard Irminsul. The skies over Khaenri'ah turned red and filled with crimson cubes, and the land was torn apart and flooded with lava.
- **The curse:** Ronova cursed pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns with immortality and turned those of mixed or foreign descent into hilichurls and monsters. Hilichurl numbers surged across Teyvat afterwards. The hilichurl archive calls the disaster a "pitch-black calamity".
- **Rhinedottir's creatures:** monsters made by "Gold" Rhinedottir, among them the dragon Durin, the Riftwolves and Bakunawa, rampaged through the nations.

Present: As of 7.1: Khaenri'ah's fate and King Irmin's are still unknown. The Curse of Immortality still binds Dainsleif and other pure-blooded survivors. The Heavenly Principles still sleep. In Snezhnaya, Ronova, who cast the curse, has lost her Authority and apparently died.

In 7.1 (Archon Quest Chapter VII Act IV), Rhinedottir revealed that the Third Descender, Saarelainen, had bound the Heavenly Principles with a curse that would trigger if they ever harmed his and Anastasya's descendants, the Khaenri'ahns. Anastasya concluded that the cataclysm triggered it, which explains the Principles' sleep. The same quest presents the Curse of Immortality as a permanent judgment laid under the Heavenly Principles' authority. Unlike Ronova's Curse of Death on Snezhnaya, it was not undone when her Authority was revoked.

79.content: During the cataclysm, while the Knights of Favonius were away on Grand Master Arundolyn's expedition against the monsters, the dark dragon Durin attacked Mondstadt. Rhinedottir had created him and sent him to Teyvat to "display his beauty". He seems to have been unaware of the destruction he caused. Mondstadt's people prayed, and Barbatos woke and called on Dvalin. Together they fought Durin over Dragonspine, which Barbatos chose as his burial place to contain his poison. Durin fell there and Dvalin swallowed his Abyss-tainted blood. Dvalin then slept in Old Mondstadt to recover.

80.comment: Cataclysm: The Chasm and Dunyu in the cataclysm
80.content: In Liyue, monsters poured out of the Chasm. Morax sent the Millelith to defend and evacuate the miners. Bosacius, a yaksha who had once abandoned his post after going mad from karma, returned to fight beside them. He, the exorcist Boyang and the Millelith vanguard lured the monsters deep underground and sealed them in the Chasm's Bed with the Fantastic Compass, dying in the process. Liyue won, at heavy cost. The people of Dunyu left their town for Liyue Harbor; why remains unspoken.

81.content: Makoto, then Electro Archon, went to Khaenri'ah and was slain there, dying in Ei's arms. In Inazuma, Ei, Mikoshi Chiyo, the Kitsune Saiguu, Reizenbou and Takamine the Mistsplitter fought the dark forces. Chiyo was swallowed by a "beast of sin", killed it from within, was corrupted, and turned on Ei, who cut off her horns and sword arm. The Kitsune Saiguu was consumed by the darkness. Takamine vanished in battle, resurfacing years later only to die at the hands of his lover Asase Hibiki. Ei became Archon, and the losses drove her pursuit of Eternity.

82.comment: Cataclysm: Sumeru and the desert in the cataclysm
82.content: Rukkhadevata stayed behind to guard Irminsul while the rest of The Seven went to Khaenri'ah, but forbidden knowledge surged into Irminsul and into her. She died stalling it and created Nahida as her successor. In the desert, monsters tore a great rift, Tunigi Hollow. The Hydro Archon Egeria fell there, and her body became the Amrita of Vourukasha Oasis. Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm to anchor Egeria's tainted consciousness and contain the defilement. The bird Simurgh gave her life purifying the Amrita, and the Pari were born from her. The Pari, the Darshan of Nagarjuna, Dainsleif and the Khaenri'ahn Schwanenritter all fought the Abyss there.

83.content: With Egeria dead, Focalors became Hydro Archon, and the Oceanids, rejecting her, left Fontaine. The great beast Elynas appeared and polluted land and sea. Basil Elton, vice-director of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, led the Fontaine Armada after it. For 35 days the fleet chased Elynas while drawing Abyssal sea creatures, then rammed him, dying to a man. Elynas later died of his wounds; the Melusines were born from his remains.
