84.content: Natlan suffered more than any nation because its Ley Lines were shallow. Rhinedottir's creature Bakunawa wiped out Tenochtzitoc. Tenoch rallied heroes from the six tribes, and Mavuika became Pyro Archon and joined them. At what became the Mare Jivari, Tenoch let himself be devoured so Sanhaj could shatter Bakunawa. The Children of Echoes, aided by the Khaenri'ahn soldiers Zephaniah and Irizar, sealed the Abyss underground with Shadow Pins. The Abyss took root in the Night Kingdom, beginning the Night Warden Wars. Mavuika placed her life in the Sacred Flame to return after five hundred years.

85.comment: Cataclysm: Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai in the cataclysm
85.content: Nod-Krai was the first land struck after Khaenri'ah, and neither Snezhnaya's court nor the gods defended it. Solovei the Torchforger and Aila, the first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, turned the tide with the moons' power and founded the Lightkeepers. Aila gave Solovei the Arrow of Terpikeraunas. The Wild Hunt has plagued Nod-Krai ever since. After the cataclysm the Tsaritsa granted Nod-Krai autonomy under the Lightkeepers.

86.comment: Cataclysm: The twins in the cataclysm
86.content: The twins had crash-landed in Teyvat. The sibling woke first, reached Khaenri'ah and was named heir, then witnessed its destruction. They woke the Traveler and tried to leave the world. Asmoday, calling herself the Sustainer of the Heavenly Principles, blocked them and denounced "the arrogation of mankind". She sealed the sibling first, then the Traveler, in dark red cubes. The Traveler slept for five hundred years with their powers sealed; the sibling woke earlier and travelled with Dainsleif.

87.comment: Cataclysm: Third Descender's curse and the slumber
87.content: Long before the cataclysm, Saarelainen agreed to be split into the seven Gnoses in exchange for Anastasya's resurrection and a promise that the Heavenly Principles would never harm their descendants, the Khaenri'ahns. He bound the promise with a curse that would trigger if it were broken. Revealing this in 7.1, Rhinedottir led Anastasya to conclude that the Principles' attack in the cataclysm set the curse off. That is why they have slept for five hundred years.

88.content:
Chichen Uctokah (also: Land of Seven Flames, Chichen Uctokah dragon city): Chichen Uctokah, called the Land of Seven Flames, was a city built by dragons in what is now Natlan. Its sovereign was the Dragonlord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L, whom Paimon nicknames Ixlel. The human usurper Och-Kan later seized the city and tried to found his empire, Ochkanatlan, on it.

The dragons also built it as the base of a "stairway", more precisely a cable, meant to reach beyond Teyvat's sky, working together with the satellite later known as the Tonatiuh. Its ruler survives only as a voice trapped in a statue.

Established: - Chichen Uctokah is named by its ruler as the "Land of Seven Flames", and she calls herself its sovereign, a Dragonlord.
- Its ruler was the Dragonlord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L, who gives a longer technical-sounding designation as well. Paimon shortens the name to Ixlel and the Dragonlord accepts it grudgingly.
- Och-Kan, called the usurper, tried to build his nation Ochkanatlan upon the city.
- Ixlel says that her authority was stolen and that her memories were used to entrap her. She says he forced her to serve his empire because he did not know how to run the city. Her heart was broken apart and hidden in devices.
- The empire and its delusions are said to have fallen to ash, while Ixlel remained imprisoned in a crude statue in the Old Core of Chu'ulel, her life nearly spent.

Accounts: - Ixlel's version: a great Dragonlord betrayed and enslaved by a traitor who stole her authority. She is proud, theatrical and bitter, so her tale carries her own grievance.
- Kukulkan's version: the city and its cable belonged to the dragons' project to reach beyond the sky. He treats Och-Kan as a failed experiment in merging human and dragon, and his words serve his own plan.

Open questions: - How large the city was, who lived in it, and when it fell are not stated.
- What the Land of Seven Flames refers to (seven flames or seven districts) is never explained.
- The identity of the other lost rulers Ixlel mentions is not given.

Connections: - Ochkanatlan was raised over this city; see the Ochkanatlan civilisation entry, and the Old Core of Chu'ulel where Ixlel is kept.
- The Tonatiuh, the sky-ship tied to the cable, and the Abyss Order's use of Ochkanatlan's ruins are part of the same story.
- The Thirteen Sovereign Lords and the false sky are the wider setting for the Dragonlords' attempts to reach beyond the sky.

89.comment: Chichen Uctokah: Land of Seven Flames
89.content: Chichen Uctokah, the Land of Seven Flames, is the dragon city that Ixlel (Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L) once ruled. Och-Kan seized it and built Ochkanatlan upon it. The dragons had also built it as the base of a sky cable reaching beyond Teyvat, alongside the satellite Tonatiuh. Details of the city itself are sparse in canon.

key: Heavenly Principles' conquest of the dragons
90.content:
Conquest of the Seven Sovereigns (also: When the Doves Held Branches, war against the Seven Sovereigns, Heavenly Principles' conquest of the dragons, usurpation of the dragons' Authorities): The oldest conflict in Teyvat's recorded lore. An Enkanomiyan chronicle calls the era "When the Doves Held Branches". The eternal throne of the heavens, the Heavenly Principles or Primordial One, came to the world, made four shining shades of itself and fought the Seven Sovereigns, the dragon-lords of the old world. After forty years the Sovereigns were vanquished. The invader took part of their elemental Authorities and reshaped the old Light Realm into the Human Realm. Followers of the defeated Sovereigns fled into the sea, and the stolen power later became the basis of the Archons' thrones.

This conquest is distinct from the later war of funerary flame, when the Dragon King Nibelung returned with Abyssal power to fight the same usurper, and from the Archon War, fought over the thrones made from the stolen power. It explains why surviving Sovereigns such as Dvalin, Apep and Neuvillette cannot use their full power while an Archon holds the matching Authority.

Established: - Before the Heavenly Principles arrived, the world belonged to the dragons. The Dragon King Nibelung and the Seven Sovereigns led it, and each Sovereign held one elemental Authority and a region attuned to that element (Seven Sovereigns wiki, drawing on Before Sun and Moon).
- The chronicle Before Sun and Moon (The Byakuyakoku Collection, Vol. 2) says the eternal throne of the heavens came and the world was made anew. The Primordial One then fought the seven "terrifying sovereigns" and made four shining shades of itself.
- Later quests and the Four Shades page name those Shades as Naberius (Life), Ronova (Death), Istaroth (Time) and Asmoday (Space).
- The chronicle says forty winters entombed the flames and forty summers churned the seas, after which the Sovereigns were vanquished and "the seven nations submitted to the heavens".
- The victor then began making heaven and earth for humanity. The seas accepted those who rebelled and would not kneel, so the Sovereigns' followers came to live in the Dark Sea and deep water.
- In Calamitous Tread (4.1) Neuvillette tells the Traveler and Paimon that when the First Usurper arrived on Teyvat it seized a part of the dragons' power, and that this stolen power is the basis of the Archons' Authorities. Seven elemental Archons correspond to seven Sovereigns.

Accounts: - The Enkanomiyan chronicle tells it as a divine conquest from a scribe's point of view: heaven's will taking shape on earth, with the Primordial One as the true lord.
- Neuvillette calls the invader the "First Usurper" and treats the Authorities as stolen. This is a dragon's view.
- Apep, in the quest Homecoming, is at first hostile to anyone tied to the old world's usurpers and remains dissatisfied with the current order even after calming down.
- The Heavenly Principles give no account of the event in anything the Traveler hears.

Open questions: - How exactly the Authorities were divided: how much stayed with the Sovereigns and how much went to the thrones.
- Whether there was an Electro Sovereign and what became of it.
- Who the original Anemo and Hydro Sovereigns were.
- Why the Heavenly Principles chose Teyvat, beyond a home for humanity, and what became of the Sovereigns' domains.
- Whether the forty years are literal.

Connections: - Aftermath: the Heavenly Principles create humanity about 400 years later and the unified civilization begins (lore.unified-civilization).
- Second conflict: Nibelung returns with Abyssal power and is killed by the Heavenly Principles; that war ended about 6,000 years ago (lore.war-of-funerary-flame).
- The stolen Authorities become the divine thrones that gods fight over in the Archon War (lore.archon-war, cosmology.gnosis).
- Present day as of 7.1: Neuvillette (Hydro, Fontaine, Authority restored after Focalors' death), Dvalin (Anemo, Mondstadt), Apep (Dendro, Sumeru) and Azhdaha (Geo, Liyue) survive; Xiuhcoatl was killed by Xbalanque and the Cryo Sovereign is dead.

key: Forty Years After the Held Branches
91.comment: Conquest of the Seven Sovereigns: When the Doves Held Branches
91.content: The Enkanomiyan chronicle Before Sun and Moon names the age of the Heavenly Principles' war on the Seven Sovereigns "When the Doves Held Branches". It records that the Primordial One made four shades of itself, that forty winters and forty summers followed, and that the Sovereigns were then vanquished and the seven nations submitted to the heavens. The same book dates the creation of humans to 400 years after the Held Branches.

92.comment: Conquest of the Seven Sovereigns: The Seven Sovereigns
92.content: The Seven Sovereigns were the mightiest dragons of the Light Realm, each holding one elemental Authority and ruling a region. Canon names Dvalin (Anemo, successor), Azhdaha (Geo), Apep (Dendro), Neuvillette (Hydro, successor to the first Hydro Dragon), Xiuhcoatl (Pyro, killed) and an unnamed Cryo Dragon (dead). No Electro Sovereign is identified. Part of their Authorities became the Archons' powers.

93.content:
Curse of Khaenri'ah (also: Curse of Immortality, Curse of the Khaenri'ahns, Khaenri'ahn curse, curse of the wilderness, Ronova's curse): When the gods destroyed Khaenri'ah about 500 years ago, Ronova, the Ruler of Death, laid a curse on its people. Those of pure Khaenri'ahn blood received the Curse of Immortality: they cannot die, yet their bodies and minds keep eroding. Those whose ancestry came from the lands of other gods received the "curse of the wilderness" and became monsters, hilichurls among them.

Ronova herself was defeated in 7.1, but the Curse of Immortality was not lifted: the Traveler concludes it was a permanent curse set under the Heavenly Principles' judgment, which she could not undo at will. Her separate Curse of Death over Snezhnaya ended with her Authority.

Established: - Cast as Khaenri'ah fell, by Ronova, one of the Four Shades.
- Pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns, the "greater sinners", were made immortal; people of other gods' ancestry were turned into monsters.
- Immortal does not mean unharmed: body and soul keep eroding.

- Eide (Chlothar Alberich), whom the Traveler meets through their sibling's memories of Avidya Forest in the Caribert act (3.5), called the curse a "gift" from the gods that took away any chance of release. His son Caribert, whose mother came from Mondstadt, turned into a hilichurl.
- People with strong Khaenri'ahn blood can be recognised by their eyes. In 7.1 Mitya also sensed the "signature" of the Curse of Immortality on Dainsleif and on Pierro.

Immortality: The Curse of Immortality is laid on pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns. Capitano calls it "the curse of absolute life". They cannot die, but Dainsleif says that over time both body and soul wear down until they are nearly nonexistent.

Dainsleif is the clearest case, and he carries a ring from his brother Vedrfolnir that keeps resetting his body's condition, which has preserved him far better than other immortals such as Capitano, whose decay was severe after centuries. Even so, his mind is still affected by erosion.

Wilderness: The curse of the wilderness falls on Khaenri'ahns whose ancestry belonged to other gods' lands. It turns them into monsters, including hilichurls: they lose their language and most of their memory and sink into a painful, prolonged existence.

Eide explains the rule: Khaenri'ah began as a single bloodline but welcomed any human who forsook their gods, and those people were punished with the curse of the wilderness as they fled. Caribert, whose mother was from Mondstadt, was one such case. Dainsleif confirms that the hilichurls in the Chasm are former citizens of Khaenri'ah.

Ronova and the curse: Ronova is the Ruler of Death, one of the four gods the Heavenly Principles created. In Pierro's memory she cast the Curse of Immortality with no pity and no pleasure, only indifference, while people begged for mercy. In 5.3 Capitano used the curse against her (see Capitano's Gambit); she chose to keep it.

Bearers: Known cursed Khaenri'ahns as of 7.1:
- Dainsleif, the Bough Keeper, who wanders Teyvat and hunts the Abyss Order.
- Capitano (Thrain), First of the Fatui Harbingers, whose body now lies seated on the Throne of the Primal Fire after he merged his life force with the Lord of the Night.
- Pierro, Director of the Fatui, who in his earlier life as Eftirvit was among those cursed as he looked on Ronova.
- Eide, who is Chlothar Alberich, pure-blooded and cursed with immortality; the skeletons later found in Avidya Forest leave his end uncertain.
- Halfdan, the Black Serpent Knights and the hilichurls of the Chasm, cursed in the wilderness form.

In the world today: The Abyss Order learned of a pool in the Chasm that eases the curse. In the world quest series including Requiem of the Echoing Depths (2.6), the sibling authorised an experimental device to amplify it, despite a low chance of success and a high chance of causing suffering. Dainsleif and the Traveler stopped it, with Halfdan sacrificing himself to halt the device. Dainsleif told Halfdan's spirit a comforting lie, that Khaenri'ah still stood, so that he could pass on in peace.

Open questions: - Whether and how the curse could ever end.
- How Kaeya and Rhinedottir escaped it, if they did.
- How the ring of Vedrfolnir works.

Connections: See Fall of Khaenri'ah, Cataclysm, Fall of Ronova, Ronova, the Four Shades, Dainsleif, Capitano, Pierro, hilichurls, the Abyss Order, Erosion and the Heavenly Principles' dormancy.

94.content:
Destruction of Irminsul (also: Burning of Irminsul, burning of the World Tree, Irminsul crisis, Irminsul's destruction): The destruction of Irminsul is the climax of the Sumeru part of Song of the Welkin Moon (Archon Quest Acts IX and X, Version 6.6). After his body died in Nod-Krai, Dottore reached Irminsul through the Ley Lines and took it over from inside, putting Nahida into a coma and making a giant Irminsul tree rise in Sumeru City. Sumeru moved the world's information into Aaru. Nahida then invoked her authority as Irminsul's keeper and burned the tree with the Pyro Gnosis, which Mavuika had given her. The Shades Ronova, Istaroth and Naberius consented. Dottore died in the fire, and as of 7.1 Aaru does Irminsul's work.

The fire burned for seven days and seven nights, and only the underground parts of the tree remained. Nahida says Teyvat's most vital information was largely preserved. Her own link was moved from Irminsul to Aaru by Nicole, so she was not harmed. The Pyro Gnosis vanished in the fire. Nahida says that with Irminsul burned, the flow of fate now "carries many more possibilities."

Course: - Warning: Collei dreamed that everyone in Sumeru City had swapped identities and only she remembered the truth. Nicole spoke into her mind and called it a premonition. Nahida and the new Sages evacuated the rainforest to Caravan Ribat.
- Collapse: Irminsul stopped recording and processing information. Nahida took over the work herself until she fell into a coma. She was moved away to weaken her link, and Apep sheltered her at the Heart of Oasis and shared Dendro energy with her.
- Spreading madness: civilians who tried to return near the Yasna Monument fell into psychosis and killed one another, and abnormal Ley Line Blossoms appeared. The Jinn rose around Gurabad until Liloupar calmed them, and a barrier sealed Sumeru off.
- Aaru: the Seven Pillars agreed to open Aaru after Nefer answered Deshret's three questions ("time"), freeing Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf. The Akademiya's scholars, led by Alhaitham and Kaveh, rebuilt Aaru and merged it with the Akasha.
- The tree: a colossal silver Irminsul tree burst up in Sumeru City. Nahida called it "a tree of unbridled greed" and took it as proof that Dottore was behind the crisis.

The burning: Dottore broke the ground under them and the three fell into Irminsul's depths. Nahida drew the Pyro Gnosis out of the Traveler and declared, "I invoke my supreme authority as the keeper of Irminsul," asking the Shades to commend or condemn her. Ronova, the Ruler of Death, asked whether she would destroy what was both her roots and her finest achievement. Nahida answered that Irminsul was corrupted beyond redemption and that she honoured it by fighting for the humanity it exists to protect. Istaroth reminded her that the Archons owe their authority to the Heavenly Principles. Naberius gave the verdict: since Nahida had become "a great tree" herself, the loss of another tree was nothing to fear. The Pyro Gnosis burst into flame and set Irminsul's roots alight.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): set after 6.6, Sumeru is rebuilding from a crisis everyone in the nation lived through: evacuation, the sealed border, the madness near the city, the giant tree and its burning. Most Sumerians know Irminsul burned and that their Archon is recovering. The details (Dottore's soul, the Shades, the Pyro Gnosis) are known only to those who were inside or in the leadership.

95.comment: Destruction of Irminsul: Dottore inside Irminsul
95.content: After his body died in Nod-Krai, Dottore entered Irminsul through death. Pantalone placed his final data backup into the Ley Lines, and the two halves of him merged inside the tree. From there he restricted Nahida's authority, watched the world through Irminsul, and grew a giant Irminsul tree in Sumeru City. He died when Nahida burned Irminsul with the Pyro Gnosis in 6.6, pulled into the fire by his own deleted Segments.

96.content: When Dottore's invasion put Irminsul in grave danger, a rule laid down by the Heavenly Principles sealed Sumeru inside a barrier so that the rest of the world could survive even if Sumeru fell. Nicole and Nefer got in just before it closed. Only the Traveler, who has no records in Irminsul, could walk through it, which is how the Pyro Gnosis was brought in from Natlan.

97.content:
Eleazar (also: Eleazar disease, Eleazar patients): Treat Eleazar as a past-tense disease: before that Archon Quest it was a feared, incurable condition tied to forbidden knowledge, and it has since disappeared. Hospital records note that some patients (the "Specimens") believed it was divine punishment, and desperate families sometimes grasped at false promises of a cure.

Established: - Hospital research notes say sufferers carry a higher elemental content than ordinary people, and that managing and reducing it can control the disease. The unnamed researcher found one treatment that made a late-stage patient's symptoms vanish entirely.
- Nilotpala Lotus can help patients regain energy, and Sumeru's forests are said to ease the illness, though the Withering made the disease noticeably worse.
- Some people were born with it: Collei and Dunyarzad are given as examples. A boy named Arbaaz, described as "little", is recorded at the hospital.
- Cases were increasing in Sumeru City, and residents with symptoms were urged to go to the Bimarstan.

Accounts: - The Akademiya built a hospital at Dar al-Shifa in the Great Red Sand to study and treat Eleazar. Its doctor found a working treatment using an unknown material. The records mention "Specimens" who called the treatment blasphemous, because they believed the illness was divine punishment. The hospital was later abandoned for undisclosed reasons and the Akademiya barred access to the ruins.
- The Fatui under Il Dottore also researched treatments using a god's remains. One of his subordinates falsely told parents the Fatui had a cure, collecting afflicted children as test subjects; Collei was among those handed over (Tighnari, in Chronic Illness, says her mother did so after a Fatui member lied about having a cure).

Open questions: - What triggers Eleazar in an individual is not stated.
- Whether the Fatui used the Dar al-Shifa hospital or a different desert site is unclear.
- The identity of the Dar al-Shifa doctor is scrubbed from the records.

Connections: - The Withering: Eleazar is the form it takes in human bodies.
- King Deshret: Kasala's memories show a strikingly similar affliction in his day: darkened scales and crazed whispers in people's minds after forbidden knowledge reached them. Rukkhadevata helped erase the knowledge, and Deshret sealed it away at the cost of his life and his civilisation.
- Irminsul: once Rukkhadevata's tainted consciousness was removed, the symptoms disappeared and patients recovered within days.

98.content: An Akademiya hospital in the Great Red Sand built to study and treat Eleazar. It is now abandoned and closed to the public by the Akademiya. Documents left behind include a diagnostic report linking Eleazar to high elemental content, a record of a treatment that worked, and Abbas's account of fleeing after surviving it.

99.content:
Fall of Khaenri'ah (also: destruction of Khaenri'ah, Khaenri'ah's destruction, fall of Khaenriah, Khaenri'ah's fall): Five hundred years ago Khaenri'ah, an underground kingdom built entirely by humans with no god, was destroyed. Its last king, the Vinster King Irmin, grew obsessed with the power of the Abyss. He named the Traveler's twin his heir and "Savior", then used them as a vessel to absorb Abyssal power. A palace coup led by Dainsleif ended with five of Khaenri'ah's greatest figures, the Five Sinners, dividing that power among themselves. Then the gods came: the Heavenly Principles and The Seven laid the kingdom waste, and Ronova cursed its people. The fall is the core of the cataclysm, and its survivors went on to found the Abyss Order and help found the Fatui.

Version 7.1 revealed a final twist. The Khaenri'ahns descend from the Tsaritsa Anastasya and the Third Descender, Saarelainen, who long ago bound the Heavenly Principles with a curse in case they ever harmed his descendants. Destroying Khaenri'ah triggered it, and the Heavenly Principles have been asleep ever since.

Established: - Khaenri'ah was a godless kingdom of humans, called by Dainsleif "the pride of humankind". It lay underground beneath what is now Sumeru.
- About 500 years ago it was destroyed "by gods". The Traveler and their sibling, newly fallen into Teyvat, saw it burn.
- Pure-blooded survivors were cursed with immortality by Ronova, the Ruler of Death. Many others became monsters, and some of their descendants are the hilichurls and the Abyss Order.

- Under the Eclipse Dynasty, Khaenri'ah built machines meant to fight Celestia. Ruin Guards were once called "Field Tillers", after the saying that land is won with "steel and blood", not farming tools. A letter found in the Gavireh Lajavard ruins says the kingdom's "four pillars" prospered by "spying upon secrets from beyond the skies". This let their machines escape the world's laws.
- Every Archon except Rukkhadevata was summoned to Khaenri'ah during the disaster. She stayed to guard Irminsul from the forbidden knowledge flooding it.
- Ei says Makoto, the Electro Archon of the time, went to Khaenri'ah alone without telling her and never came back.

The road to ruin: Irmin, the last Vinster King of the Eclipse Dynasty, began as a sane ruler. His closest counsellors were Vedrfolnir, "The Visionary", and Hroptatyr, "The Wise". Over time he became fixated on the Abyss. The Universitas Magistrorum moved almost all its staff into Abyssal Energy research. He also ordered every descendant of the earlier Crimson Moon Dynasty hunted down, as threats to his line.

The coup: Vedrfolnir warned Irmin that if he kept on this path, Khaenri'ah would fall. The king had his eyes gouged out and threw him into a cell. Dainsleif, captain of the royal guard and Vedrfolnir's younger brother, gathered Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir ("Gold"), Surtalogi ("The Foul") and Rerir to storm the palace that night and free him. Dainsleif said he did not want treason; he meant to make the king see his error with his sword. But once inside, the others turned on his plan. Each took a share of the Abyssal power the king had poured into the sibling, and they became the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah. Dainsleif says they each fell to their own desire: Vedrfolnir to foresee the future, Hroptatyr to limitless knowledge, Rhinedottir to creating life, Surtalogi to supreme strength.

The destruction: The gods descended on Khaenri'ah and destroyed it. The Traveler remembers a sea of flames and a god, Asmoday, who sealed the twins as they tried to leave the world.

The sibling woke first, saw the kingdom fall, then woke the Traveler and told them the destruction of Khaenri'ah had thrown the world into chaos and they should leave. Asmoday, the Ruler of Space, stopped them, calling them "outlanders", and sealed both twins. Ronova then laid the Curse of Immortality on pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns. Dainsleif was among them, condemned, in the sibling's words, to wander forever while his people became monsters of the Abyss.

Aftermath: With King Irmin "indisposed", Knight Marshal Anfortas of the Schwanenritter proclaimed himself Regent and led the final kingdom council, the Regnum Concilium Ultimum. Survivors able to travel went up to Sumeru with the Schwanenritter and their Ruin Golems. On the surface, many refugees were struck by a disease that turned them into monsters, and some who had not yet fallen ill went back underground. The Schwanenritter fought the Abyss to the last knight.

100.comment: Fall of Khaenri'ah: Vinster King Irmin
100.content: Irmin was the last Vinster King of Khaenri'ah's Eclipse Dynasty. He trusted Vedrfolnir and Hroptatyr above all, and over time became obsessed with Abyssal power. He approved technology built on "secrets from beyond the skies", purged the Crimson Moon bloodline, named the Traveler's sibling heir and "Savior", and made them a vessel for Abyssal power. He blinded Vedrfolnir for warning that Khaenri'ah would fall, which set off the palace coup.

101.comment: Fall of Khaenri'ah: The storming of the palace
101.content: On the night Vedrfolnir was blinded and imprisoned, Dainsleif, then captain of the royal guard, the "Twilight Sword", led Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir, Surtalogi and Rerir into the palace to free him. It was meant as a rescue that would force the king to see reason. Instead the five took shares of the Abyssal power held in the sibling and became the Five Sinners, leaving Dainsleif betrayed. Monsters spread through the city the same night.

102.comment: Fall of Khaenri'ah: Regent Anfortas and the exodus
102.content: Knight Marshal Anfortas of the Schwanenritter became Regent when King Irmin was "indisposed". He led the evacuation of Khaenri'ahn survivors up into Sumeru, where the knights and their Ruin Golems fought the Abyss until none were left. Many refugees on the surface fell to a disease that turned them into monsters. Sumeru's scholars remembered the knights as the "heroes of Dahri".

103.comment: Fall of Khaenri'ah: The Third Descender's curse
103.content: Saarelainen, the Third Descender, gave his body to become the seven Gnoses on condition that the Heavenly Principles restore Anastasya and never harm his descendants, the Khaenri'ahns. He secured the promise with a curse that would trigger if it was broken. When the Heavenly Principles destroyed Khaenri'ah, the curse took effect, and they have slept ever since (revealed in 7.1).

key: defeat of the Ruler of Death
104.content:
Fall of Ronova (also: death of Ronova, Ronova's defeat, defeat of the Ruler of Death, Black Feathers Scattered at Parting): The fall of Ronova is the climax of the Snezhnaya Archon Quest act "A Rekviem for the Underworld" (7.1). Ronova, the Shade who rules death, had been suppressing Snezhnaya's research with her Curse of Death. While the Tsaritsa held Rhinedottir in conversation and secretly slowed time around her with six Gnoses, Ronova's victims could not be revived in time; Celestia punished the violation by taking away Ronova's Authority of Death. The Traveler, Dainsleif and Pierro then defeated her. Mortally wounded, she fled and, dying, fused the Eitr with the Celestial Nail above the Cryo Dragon's corpse as a "parting gift". She is the first of the Four Shades shown dying.

Pierro landed the decisive blow with a new, untested Delusion called the "Eye of the Fatui", at a heavy cost to his soul and life force. The Curse of Death lifted with her Authority, freeing Project Mistilteinn, but the Curse of Immortality on the Khaenri'ahns remains. After her act, all of Teyvat's Celestial Nails began to cast strange pillars of light into the sky.

Established: - Ronova, the Ruler of Death, is one of the Four Shades created by the Heavenly Principles.
- In Snezhnaya she had imposed a Curse of Death: when someone conceived technology threatening the Heavenly Principles, they and those around them briefly died and forgot the idea.
- Those deaths broke the rules she served, so she relied on Rhinedottir, Ruler of Life, to revive the victims before Celestia's "monitoring cycle" noticed.
- The Tsaritsa broke that loophole; Celestia reclaimed Ronova's Authority, and she was defeated in battle.

- Earlier in Chapter VII (7.0), the curse caused unexplained memory loss among Armory Palace researchers working on Project Mistilteinn, including Mitya. A whole audience at the Korolevskiy Theater, the Traveler among them, was trapped in the afterlife until the Traveler and Mitya unmasked Ronova, who had disguised herself as Alyosha. Later she tried to take Paimon by force at the Armory Palace before Pierro stopped her.
- The Fatui treated a direct confrontation as inevitable and built a new Delusion for it, using Arlecchino as the base because she descends from the Crimson Moon, which once held the authority over death.
- Snezhnaya's victory, as Pierro puts it, came at the moment Celestia reclaimed her Authority; the battle afterward was the old feud of the Curse of Immortality playing out.

Battle of rankova zorya: Ronova struck Rankova Zorya and triggered the Curse of Death. The Traveler fought her (in gameplay, with Odette and Vesna as trial party members), was killed and escaped the afterlife first, drawing on Vesna's use of the Authority of Life and memories of every nation they had visited. Waking among the dead, the Traveler stalled Ronova with taunts: she was bound by more rules than she controlled, a tool of the Heavenly Principles, while Paimon was writing her own destiny. Ronova, angered, promised torment instead of death, and waited for Rhinedottir to revive the dead. The revival never came.

The tsaritsas gambit: At the palace, the Tsaritsa offered her account of sighting Asmoday, persuaded Rhinedottir to stay and finish the tea, and kept her talking. Rhinedottir eventually noticed her drink had not cooled: the Tsaritsa had used the six Gnoses as nodes to slow time in the hall, so the window for reviving Ronova's victims passed unnoticed outside. Rhinedottir said Cryo amplified by the Gnoses could affect the bounds of Reason, slowing time though not stopping it.

Parting gift: Ronova had secretly teleported away. In a final cutscene she emerges, dying, before the Nail of Retribution over the Cryo Dragon's corpse and fuses the Eitr with it as her "parting gift"; the Nail begins to crumble and she disintegrates.

The Eitr (Embryonic-Ichoric-Telluric-Rudiment) is a forbidden creation of Hyperborea hidden in the Shadow Realm. The cutscene description says Ronova, feeling death for the first time, meant all of Teyvat to share that sensation as Holy Soil spread across the land. After the quest, pillars of light rise above Teyvat's Celestial Nails.

Aftermath: Within days Rankova Zorya was being repaired, Armory Palace staff confirmed the restrictions on Project Mistilteinn were gone, and the Tsaritsa granted an audience commending everyone involved. Dainsleif attended out of respect for the "Mother of Khaenri'ah" and called the victory the start of a new era that would not be peaceful. Pierro was not seen; Dainsleif said the battle had taken an irrecoverable toll on his mind and soul.

Open questions: - What the Eitr will do to the Celestial Nails and whether Holy Soil will spread.
- Who, if anyone, now holds the Authority of Death.

Connections: See Ronova, the Four Shades, Rhinedottir, the Tsaritsa, Pierro, Dainsleif, Project Mistilteinn, Delusions, the Eitr, Celestial Nails and Holy Soil.

105.comment: Fall of Ronova: Eye of the Fatui
105.content: The Eye of the Fatui is the new Delusion completed for Pierro just in time for the battle with Ronova, developed with Arlecchino as the base for her Crimson Moon heritage. Untested in combat, it let him call down a vast elemental nail that mortally wounded Ronova, at the price of his soul and life force; Ronova said no mortal could withstand that power. Dainsleif said the toll on Pierro was irrecoverable.

106.comment: Fall of Ronova: Ronova's Curse of Death
106.content: Ronova's Curse of Death killed anyone in Snezhnaya who conceived technology threatening the Heavenly Principles, together with those near them, and erased the idea. Rhinedottir then revived them before Celestia's monitoring cycle could notice, a loophole around rules the killings broke. When the Tsaritsa delayed the revival in 7.1, the curse was exposed, Ronova lost her Authority and the curse ended with it.

107.content:
Future of Khaenri'ah (also: fate of Khaenri'ah, revival of Khaenri'ah, New Khaenri'ah, Khaenri'ah's survivors, what became of Khaenri'ah, Khaenri'ah's legacy): Khaenri'ah, the godless underground kingdom, fell about five hundred years ago, and canon has never said cleanly what became of it. Its last king, Irmin, was reported "indisposed" and the Knight Marshal Anfortas took over as regent; neither man's end is stated. Most of its pure-blooded people are cursed to live on, and the Traveler's sibling says the Abyss Order is building a "New Khaenri'ah". As of 7.1, even a Khaenri'ahn alchemist like Rhinedottir says the old kingdom "no longer exists".

This entry gathers the open threads about the kingdom's future: the fate of its rulers, the survivors and their curses, and the competing hopes of reviving it. It does not resolve any of them.

Established: - Khaenri'ah fell in the Cataclysm five hundred years ago. The gods and the Heavenly Principles were behind its destruction, the wiki's summary of canon says, as punishment for using forbidden knowledge.
- A notice found in the underground Khaenri'ahn ruins (Gavireh Lajavard, Sumeru) says King Irmin was in an "indisposed state" and the Knight Marshal Anfortas proclaimed himself temporary Regent. That is the last word on the monarchy.
- In 7.1 Rhinedottir says it is a shame that Khaenri'ah no longer exists, and she and Dainsleif both call the Tsaritsa the "Mother of Khaenri'ah".

- **The throne.** Irmin is called the last Vinster King of the Eclipse Dynasty and is known to have had one eye. The Alberich family teaching that Kaeya kept (Hidden Strife, 2.8, a limited-time event) says the Alberich Clan, which had no royal blood, "stepped in as regents when the strength of the one-eyed king Irmin failed". Anfortas is not named in that text; the link to him is the wiki's deduction.
- **The regent.** Anfortas led the Schwanenritter. The knights evacuated the able upward into Sumeru with their Ruin Golems. After surfacing, the evacuees began to sicken with an affliction that turned them into monsters, and some chose to go back underground. A coded message in Ruin Guards near Dharma Forest says the Schwanenritters fought to the last one.
- **The survivors.** Pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns were made immortal and eroded rather than dying; those with ancestry from other gods' lands became monsters, including hilichurls. The royal guards, the Black Serpent Knights, became husks or remained as changed Black Serpents.
- **The people.** In 7.1 Rhinedottir tells the Tsaritsa that all Khaenri'ahns descend from a bloodline begun with her and the Third Descender. The Tsaritsa says she was aware of this but has no memory of it.

Open questions: - Is Irmin dead, and if so how? Is he the "indisposed" king of the bulletin, or did the reports hide something?
- What became of Anfortas after the last knights fell, and did the Alberich regency outlast him?
- Can Khaenri'ah be revived, and if so where, as what, and at what cost to the people already living there?
- Does the Curse of Immortality end, and what would that mean for the surviving pure-bloods?

Connections: This is the forward-looking companion to the fall: see the Fall of Khaenri'ah and the Cataclysm for what happened, the Curse of the Khaenri'ahns for what the survivors carry, and the Traveler's Sibling's goals for the revival plan. The Heavenly Principles' dormancy and the Tsaritsa's plan explain why Snezhnaya is suddenly relevant to the kingdom's descendants.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat every statement about Khaenri'ah's future as belief or hope. Do not state that Irmin died, that Anfortas lived or died, that Khaenri'ah has been revived, or where New Khaenri'ah will stand. Characters differ: Dainsleif is sceptical, the Order is determined, and Rhinedottir is wistful. Do not use unreleased story content.

108.content: A weathered notice in the underground Khaenri'ahn ruins beneath Sumeru says that, given King Irmin's "indisposed state" and the unknown threats facing the Kingdom, Knight Marshal Anfortas proclaimed himself temporary Regent. It is the only in-world statement on the king's condition; his death, removal or survival is never stated.

109.content: Knight Marshal of the Schwanenritter. When the Cataclysm struck and Irmin was "indisposed", he declared himself Regent and took charge of the Regnum Concilium Ultimum, the Final Kingdom Council. The knights then led survivors up to Sumeru. His own fate is not stated; he appears only in documents and a hidden coded message ("In the Name of Anfortas") saying the knights fought to the last.

110.comment: Future of Khaenri'ah: Mother of Khaenri'ah
110.content: In 7.1 Rhinedottir greets the Tsaritsa Anastasya with this title and says all Khaenri'ahns descend from a bloodline begun with her and the Third Descender. Anastasya says she was aware of it, although she has no memory of it, and has never known how to face them. Dainsleif later uses the same title when he says he could not refuse her an audience.

111.content: The Traveler's sibling says the Loom of Fate has finished weaving the Ley Line network of a restored Khaenri'ah and that it is held in the Atlas of the New World. They plan to find a suitable host location for it one day, and say the nation once known as Khaenri'ah can rise again. Haden had earlier claimed the homeland was already revived and then admitted the Ley Lines were not yet complete.

112.comment: Future of Khaenri'ah: The Cursed Survivors
112.content: Pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns live on under the Curse of Immortality, eroding rather than dying. Dainsleif, Pierro and Chlothar (as Eide) are the clearest cases, along with the cursed remnants such as the Black Serpent Knights. People of mixed ancestry became monsters. As of 7.1, no cursed Khaenri'ahn has been shown freed, even after Ronova lost her authority.

113.content:
Forbidden Knowledge (also: forbidden knowledge pollution): Forbidden knowledge is a kind of knowledge that does not belong to Teyvat. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata called it a "truth" no one in the world can understand, which came from the very bottom of the Abyss. The world keeps rejecting it, and that rejection causes disasters: madness, a scale-like illness (Eleazar), and decay of the land (the Withering). It mostly struck Sumeru. Nahida and the Traveler erased it from Irminsul in 3.2.

Canon records it in King Deshret's desert kingdom thousands of years ago, in the dragon Apep, and in Irminsul and Rukkhadevata herself during the Cataclysm 500 years ago. Nahida later said the Abyss takes whatever form is most devastating to each land: in Sumeru it was forbidden knowledge, in Natlan it was monsters.

Established: - It is foreign to Teyvat and comes from the Abyss. Even the God of Wisdom could not understand it.
- People exposed to it hear "crazed whispers", go mad and grow dark grey scales. Land exposed to it loses its vigour.
- Gods and dragons can be polluted too: Apep and Rukkhadevata both were.

- Rukkhadevata warned that if it polluted Irminsul, all of Teyvat might fall apart.
- Its traces could be suppressed with divine power, contained, or altered into a more stable form, but it could not simply be destroyed. Rukkhadevata's own memory in Irminsul kept it alive after her death.
- Removing it from Irminsul (3.2) ended Eleazar within days and stopped the Withering from spreading.

History: It first afflicted the desert of King Deshret thousands of years ago, then returned with the Cataclysm 500 years ago and polluted Irminsul.

- The desert: Deshret brought it into his kingdom. Rukkhadevata saved what she could and was shrunk to a child's form by the effort; Deshret sacrificed himself, letting Apep swallow him (own entries below).
- The Cataclysm: Rukkhadevata, not summoned to Khaenri'ah because she had to protect Irminsul, felt the pollution arrive with the disaster. She built the Akasha, which used people's dreams and wisdom together with her power, and cleared almost all of it from Irminsul, but she herself was already polluted and died.
- 3.2: Nahida, the purest branch of Irminsul Rukkhadevata chose as her next incarnation, used two Gnoses to reach her predecessor's consciousness and removed Rukkhadevata from Irminsul. Everyone forgot Rukkhadevata, except the Traveler.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 forbidden knowledge is considered gone: erased from Irminsul in 3.2, so the Withering and Eleazar no longer spread. The Abyss itself remains active in other forms.

In Etched in Time (7.1), the Traveler argued that Hroptatyr's sealed notebook was no longer dangerous for this reason. Pierro agreed, and after the Harbingers voted to unseal it, he found most of its pages blank, "presumably forbidden knowledge that has been erased". What was left were Hroptatyr's personal thoughts and research notes from the Universitas Magistrorum.

Effects: - Eleazar: dark, hardened scales, numbness, nerve damage, immobility, coma, death. It was unique to Sumeru and had no cure until 3.2.
- The Withering: zones of decay in Sumeru's forests.
- Madness: "crazed whispers" in people's minds.

Connections: Source: the Abyss. Opponent: the Heavenly Principles and its Celestial Nails. Medium: Irminsul, which records knowledge and memory. Victims: King Deshret's civilisation, Apep, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Sumeru's Eleazar patients. Ended by: Nahida and the Traveler. Related phenomena with their own entries: the Withering, Eleazar, Abyssal corruption, the Akasha, the war of funerary flame, the Cataclysm.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): keep its content unknowable. Never write out what forbidden knowledge "says"; show its weight instead: whispers that half make sense, a scholar who will not stop writing, scales spreading on skin, colour draining from leaves. Present-day (7.1) Sumerians may know Eleazar is gone and the Withering has stopped, but most do not know why, and no one remembers Rukkhadevata.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): - It is not ordinary "banned research" or Akademiya censorship: it is Abyssal corruption that harms whoever holds it.
- Do not have it still spreading in Sumeru after 3.2, or have anyone except the Traveler remember Rukkhadevata.
- Do not present the Khaenri'ah connection as confirmed; canon only implies it.
- "The apocalypse" in Homecoming means this corruption inside Apep, not the end of the world.

114.comment: Forbidden Knowledge: King Deshret's forbidden knowledge
114.content: Thousands of years ago King Deshret (Al-Ahmar) brought forbidden knowledge into his desert kingdom while trying to defy the Heavenly Principles. It spread like a plague: crazed whispers, dark grey scales, dying land. His old friend Greater Lord Rukkhadevata had the priests build temples and filled them with the divine power of life. This slowed the disaster, but exhausted her until her form became a small child's. The survivors' descendants live in Aaru Village. The king finally sacrificed himself. The priest Kasala's recorded memory of this, shown in Secret of the Scorching Desert (3.1), told the desert people that the two gods had been allies, not enemies.

115.content: In Nahida's Story Quest Homecoming (3.6), Apep tells how she was polluted. The dragons once believed only forbidden knowledge could defeat the Heavenly Principles; after Nibelung's death she kept collecting it until a Celestial Nail stopped her. Swallowing King Deshret gave her his corrupted knowledge, "the apocalypse", which magnified her hatred. Elemental lifeforms born from her fled; their deaths are tied to the Withering. In the Chasm, the Spiritstone's power had turned the apocalypse into Oozing Filth, more stable but still dangerous. Nahida and the Traveler healed Apep. She grew calmer but still despises humanity.

116.comment: Forbidden Knowledge: Rukkhadevata and Irminsul's pollution
116.content: When the Cataclysm struck 500 years ago, forbidden knowledge polluted Irminsul. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata stayed behind to protect the tree and built the Akasha to clear it using the wisdom in people's dreams together with her own power. Almost all of it was removed, but she was polluted herself; even dead, her memory in Irminsul kept the corruption alive, causing the Withering and Eleazar. She chose the purest branch of Irminsul as her next incarnation, Nahida, and left her clues. In Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies (3.2), Nahida and the Traveler used two Gnoses to reach her and removed her from Irminsul. Everyone except the Traveler forgot her, and the disease and decay ended.

117.content: Before he abandoned his humanity, the Khaenri'ahn Sinner Hroptatyr ("The Wise") gave his fellow student and rival Eftirvit (both studied under Professor Mimameith), later Pierro, a notebook. When Pierro eventually read it, he realised its contents would drive him mad and could bring disaster on a national scale. With the Tsaritsa's approval the Harbingers sealed it deep in the Armory Palace archives, to be opened only by a unanimous vote of all active Harbingers. In Etched in Time (7.1), the Traveler explained that forbidden knowledge had been erased from Irminsul. The Harbingers voted to unseal it, and most pages were blank. What survived included Hroptatyr's notes on extracting the Crimson Moon's authority over Death, a discovery he first named the "blessing of immortality" and then renamed the "Curse of Immortality".

key: Plains of the Returning and Departing
118.content:
Guili Assembly (also: Guili, Plains of the Returning and Departing, Guizhong-Zhongli Assembly): The Guili Assembly was an ancient Liyue civilisation founded and ruled jointly by the God of Dust, Guizhong, and the God of Geo, Morax (later Rex Lapis, today the mortal consultant Zhongli), with the god Marchosius and the adepti at their side. Its heart was Guili Plains north of Mt. Tianheng, a land of farms and fields. About 3,700 years ago a battle of the Archon War killed Guizhong and a flood destroyed the Assembly; Morax led the survivors south and founded Liyue Harbor.

Its name joins one character each from Guizhong's name and from the name Morax then used. Today it survives as ruins, stone tablets and the memories of the long-lived.

Established: When Morax first descended, according to the tablets, he lowered the tides, raised Mt. Tianheng and calmed the seas, and the people mined jade from the mountain and built a settlement. Guizhong, called the Lord of Dust, became his ally. She and the adepti, Cloud Retainer among them, raised the Guizhong Ballista, an automatic crossbow guarding the land around Mt. Tianheng, and she brought her people north of the mountain, where they learned to farm. The fields and farming towns spread so far that one could reputedly walk to the Stone Gate along the paths between them. She named the land the Plains of the Returning and Departing (Guili Plains): her people had left their old home and, content here, had in a sense returned home. The tablets say the Lord of Rock praised her work. Marchosius, God of the Stove, is named as a third ruler and supporter in Madame Ping's retelling.

Fall: When the gods of Teyvat fought for dominance, the adepti defended Guili Plains but could not stop the tide of war, which ravaged the plains and killed Guizhong. A great flood followed that swept through the area, including Dihua Marsh. The people were scattered; Morax took them south of Mt. Tianheng, and with Marchosius and the adepti they travelled for ten days or more through a storm. They settled at what became Liyue Harbor, about 3,700 years ago. The plains were left a wilderness; a viewpoint description calls the place a once-thriving city where a certain flower bloomed in abundance, an earthly paradise consumed by war.

Legacy: The Assembly is the direct predecessor of Liyue Harbor, founded by the same survivors and the same god. Guili Plains still holds ruins, stone tablets and jade plates, and the Guizhong Ballista still stands at Mt. Tianheng. The tablets record that, after Rex Lapis pacified the warring gods, merchants and craftsmen formed the Qixing and the Millelith guarded the land. Zhongli, in the present, is a living memory of this era.

Open questions: The sources reviewed leave unanswered who killed Guizhong and how, what Morax was called at the time, why Guizhong moved to Morax's settlement, and how large the Assembly really was. Treat them as open; do not supply an invented villain or battle.

key: Plains of the Returning and Departing
119.content: Guili Plains, in the Qiongji Estuary area of Liyue, was the central region of the Guili Assembly. Today it is wild country with ruins, hilichurls and treasure hoarders, stone tablets and jade plates bearing writing, and a viewpoint called the Ruins of Guili. The name means Plains of the Returning and Departing.

120.content: Guizhong, divine name Haagentus, was the God of Dust and co-ruler of the Guili Assembly. She appeared as a young woman with long billowing sleeves, was a mechanist who taught her people farming and built the Guizhong Ballista, and died in the Archon War.

121.content: Marchosius, the God of the Stove, is named as an ally who supported the Assembly and, in a Moonlight Merriment event telling by Madame Ping, as a god devoted to the people who stayed with them during the flight to Liyue Harbor. His story is told in an event and is not common knowledge.

122.content:
Slumber of the Heavenly Principles (also: Heavenly Principles' slumber, Heavenly Principles are dormant, dormancy of the Heavenly Principles, Heavenly Principles asleep, Saarelainen's curse): The Heavenly Principles, the ruler of Celestia and First Descender, have been dormant since the Cataclysm in Khaenri'ah about 500 years ago. The best-supported explanation is a curse laid by the Third Descender, Saarelainen, which triggered when they harmed his descendants the Khaenri'ahns. Their rules and Celestia's machinery still operate, and nobody in canon knows whether they will wake.

Powers across Teyvat have used the silence: the Fatui and the Abyss Order both plot against Celestia, and the Shades act cautiously "within the rules" rather than freely. The cause is not fully confirmed in-game: the 7.1 account is partly an inference voiced by Anastasya.

Established: - About 500 years ago, during the Cataclysm in Khaenri'ah, the Heavenly Principles became involved, sending the Seven (except the Dendro Archon) and the Four Shades. Ronova cursed pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns with immortality, which the Traveler in 7.1 reads as done under the Heavenly Principles' judgment.
- Since then they have lain dormant, and no quest shows them acting directly.

- Earlier, the Heavenly Principles consolidated their rule after the War of Funerary Flame by sacrificing the Third Descender, Saarelainen, whose body became the seven Gnoses and whose existence was erased from memory.
- According to the wiki's account, Saarelainen bargained for protection of his descendants, the Khaenri'ahns, and cast a curse to guard the deal: should the Heavenly Principles harm them, they would fall into slumber.
- In 7.1 Anastasya concludes that the Cataclysm triggered that curse, which is why the Heavenly Principles are asleep. Several events since (the Hydro throne's destruction, the burning of Irminsul) have not roused them.

Accounts: - Wiki summary of the 7.1 quest Black Feathers Scattered at Parting: the Cataclysm intervention triggered Saarelainen's curse, so the Heavenly Principles sleep.
- In that quest Anastasya, the Tsaritsa, infers the link after hearing Rhinedottir's account ("That's why the Heavenly Principles are asleep"); Rhinedottir answers that it was "just a story" and that she was not answering any question.

Open questions: - Will the Heavenly Principles wake, and what would break the curse?
- What exactly did Saarelainen promise, and what is in his sealed legacy (see the Third Descender's seal)?
- Which functions of Celestia run without its ruler?

Connections: The slumber links the Cataclysm and the fall of Khaenri'ah, the origin of the Gnoses, the Tsaritsa's campaign against the Heavenly Principles, the dealings of the Four Shades, and the Traveler's sibling's long-term goal.

123.comment: Slumber of the Heavenly Principles: Heavenly Principles' slumber
123.content: After the Cataclysm about 500 years ago the Heavenly Principles stopped acting directly. The wiki attributes this to Saarelainen's curse, triggered when they harmed Khaenri'ah. Anastasya only infers the link in 7.1 and Rhinedottir does not confirm it. The Shades call this period a slumber, during which Celestia only monitors them periodically. Celestia's rules and monitoring still run, so characters speak of the slumber as real but incompletely understood. Never show the Heavenly Principles waking unless a scene is explicitly non-canon.

124.comment: Slumber of the Heavenly Principles: Saarelainen's curse
124.content: Per Rhinedottir in 7.1, Saarelainen laid a curse on the Heavenly Principles when he bargained his body for Anastasya's resurrection and a promise never to harm his descendants, the Khaenri'ahns; it would take effect only if the promise was broken. The wiki says its effect is slumber, and Anastasya infers the Cataclysm triggered it. Its precise terms are not given in canon as of 7.1.

key: pillars of light over the Celestial Nails
125.content:
Holy Soil Crisis (also: Ronova's parting gift, Nail of Retribution anomaly, pillars of light over the Celestial Nails, Holy Soil threat): At the end of the Chapter VII, Act IV Archon Quest (7.1), the dying Ronova fused the Eitr with the Nail of Retribution above the Cryo Dragon's corpse in Snezhnaya as a "parting gift". The Nail began to crumble, threatening to unleash Holy Soil upon all of Teyvat, and every other Celestial Nail began to shine with a strange pillar of light. As of 7.1 nobody knows what comes next.

Characters in Snezhnaya, Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru and Natlan are watching their own Nails. Fontaine has none, and so no mark of its own.

Established: - Ronova, mortally wounded after her Authority of Death was taken from her, went to Snezhnaya's Celestial Nail, east of Snezhnograd, above the corpse of the Cryo Dragon Sovereign.
- She fused the Eitr with the Nail. It began to crumble.
- Afterwards the Celestial Nails across Teyvat each emit a strange pillar of light.

- **The Eitr.** Its full name is Embryonic-Ichoric-Telluric-Rudiment. It is a forbidden Hyperborean creation holding Light Realm power, once used to alter organisms. The Belyi Tsar found it in the Shadow Realm; later it was studied at the Hvergelmir institute.
- **The Nail.** The wiki describes Celestial Nails as seemingly indestructible (the Skyfrost Nail had splintered into shards and the Spiritstone shed a fragment, but neither crumbled away). Ronova's act is the first time one is shown crumbling apart. In the cutscene Ronova herself begins to disintegrate as she does it.
- **What was threatened.** The wiki's summary of the scene says the crumbling Nail threatens to unleash Holy Soil upon all of Teyvat, and its description of the cutscene says Ronova intended Teyvat to share the feeling of death. That intent is the narration's, not a statement made aloud by the character.
- **The world reacts.** The world quest series "The Anomaly" opens after the Archon Quest. It has one quest per region with a Nail: Snezhnaya, Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru and Natlan. In each, a known character is found watching the Nail.

Holy soil: Holy Soil is soil rich in primordial elemental power from the three realms. Dragons can thrive in it, but it is unsuitable for human life. The process of land turning into Holy Soil is the Holy Soil phenomenon. Canon gives three older accounts.

Accounts: - **Paimon and the Traveler:** suspect the whole situation may be Ronova's revenge, and say they are not in a mood to celebrate.
- **Alyosha:** the Nail started behaving strangely only after the Ruler of Death fell; however it is read, it cannot be good.
- **Mavuika:** whatever happens, the Traveler's party will not be to blame. She says Ronova and the Heavenly Principles have long used Natlan as a tool against the Abyss and the world's destruction, and most of Natlan's past disasters came from them.

Open questions: Whether Holy Soil is spreading, what the pillars of light mean, and whether the Heavenly Principles will answer are all unresolved as of 7.1.

Other open points: how the Eitr breaks a Nail, whether the Nails will fail one after another, and what the Tsaritsa and the Fatui will do. Canon shows only concern and watching.

Connections: Ronova's defeat is told in lore.fall-of-ronova, the Tsaritsa's wider confrontation with the Heavenly Principles in lore.tsaritsas-plan, and Project Mistilteinn, freed by Ronova's fall, in lore.project-mistilteinn. The Nails are described in the Celestial Nail entry, the Eitr in its own entry, and the old Holy Soil in the Holy Soil entry.

126.comment: Holy Soil Crisis: Eitr and the Broken Nail
126.content: The Eitr is a Hyperborean product holding Light Realm power. The Belyi Tsar found it in the Shadow Realm on his 446th expedition. Ronova, dying, fused it with the Nail above the Cryo Dragon's corpse east of Snezhnograd, and the Nail began to crumble. Other Nails then began to shine.

127.comment: Holy Soil Crisis: The Anomaly (Nail Pillars of Light)
127.content: After the Archon Quest, the Celestial Nails in Snezhnaya, Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru and Natlan each emit a strange pillar of light. Locals and notable figures watch them: Alyosha, Albedo, Xiao, Yae Miko, Candace and Dehya, and Mavuika. No harm is shown as of 7.1.

128.comment: Holy Soil Crisis: Hyperborea's Holy Soil
128.content: Aksinya says the out-of-control attempt to make a Primordial Human from the Cryo Dragon Sovereign's corpse turned all of Snezhnaya into Holy Soil of primordial ice, crystallising even the Ley Lines, until the Heavenly Principles sent their Nail crashing down; Hyperborea later sank into the Shadow Realm. A thousand years later the Belyi Tsar awoke from the dragon's remains.

129.comment: Holy Soil Crisis: Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri and the Holy Soil
129.content: During the limited-time event Three Realms Gateway Offering (2.5), Sangonomiya Shrine's answer to Watatsumi's Holy Soil phenomenon is shown: every few centuries someone retrieves a Bloodbranch Coral from Enkanomiya for the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri. When Kokomi performed the rite in that event it only halted the bleaching instead of reversing it, which had never happened before; the cause was traced to the Void Realm's intrusion into Enkanomiya.

130.content:
Istaroth's Intentions (also: Istaroth's motives, Ruler of Time's interference, Istaroth meddling, Istaroth's plans): Istaroth, the Ruler of Time, is the Shade that few remember, and she has repeatedly nudged history: the Nameless Bard, Zibai's soul, Enkanomiya's sun, Makoto's tree, and the meeting that made the Traveler's sibling leave Khaenri'ah. Canon never tells us what she is trying to achieve. The only reason she gives on screen is that she needs to pass the time.

Her interventions help individuals and sometimes work around the Heavenly Principles' wishes, yet she also warns people not to defy them. She is not shown as an opponent of Celestia or as a loyal servant. Treat her goals as unknown.

Established: - In the teaser The Gods' Limits (2025-07-09), Ronova asks why Istaroth bestowed history upon "them". Istaroth answers that she had to find some way to pass the time.
- In A Space and Time Without You (5.7), the Traveler's sibling concludes that Istaroth made possible the meeting between the Traveler and the Khaenri'ahn girl Direidyth, which led the sibling to abandon Khaenri'ah to seek the Traveler. The sibling asks whether she is mocking them.

- Zibai: Istaroth gave her a Moon Wheel, making her a Moon Envoy, and warned her that blocking the Celestial Nail at Lang-Gan would cost her life. Zibai chose to protect her people anyway. Istaroth then held her at the moment of death and placed the fragments of her soul in her three selves, Ziju, Zizhi and Zijiao.
- Enkanomiya: after the island sank and its prayers went unanswered by the other Shades, Istaroth alone answered and gave Aberaku the knowledge for the artificial sun later called the Dainichi Mikoshi. She became Tokoyo Ookami there.
- Mondstadt: according to the wiki, the Nameless Bard played a melody that belonged to her at Decarabian's fall, and she preserved his lost name, Venti, when Barbatos ascended.
- Inazuma: Ei suspects that Makoto's plan to plant the Sacred Sakura through time involved a higher power; the wiki identifies it as Istaroth.
- Sumeru: in the scene where Nahida burns Irminsul (6.6), Istaroth appears with Ronova and Naberius and questions Nahida before they vanish.

Accounts: - **Istaroth herself**: gives boredom as her reason (teaser). She advises Ronova that hunting for Asmoday would do more harm than good, and tells her Pierro is watching.
- **The Traveler's sibling** (5.7): treats her as the architect of the meeting with Direidyth and asks if she is mocking them.
- **Ei** (wiki summary): believes Makoto's plan relied on Istaroth.
- **Wiki** (Profile): says she considers every life equal in value and importance, and that it is unclear whether she acts out of favour for mortals or boredom.

Open questions: - What does Istaroth want, if anything beyond passing time?
- Why did she help bring about the sibling's decision to abandon Khaenri'ah?

- Does she act for mortals, for her own amusement, or for a plan across thousands of years?
- Do the Heavenly Principles know of her interventions, and would they punish them?
- Does her view of Asmoday's absence reflect knowledge she has not shared?

Connections: Her interventions touch the Traveler's sibling's goals (lore.travelers-sibling-goals), Asmoday's possible change of side (lore.asmodays-defection), the Cataclysm, and the dormancy of the Heavenly Principles. Her own profile is npc.istaroth.

131.content: Istaroth has helped the Nameless Bard, Zibai, Aberaku, Makoto and the Traveler's sibling in ways that look unrelated. Her only on-screen explanation is that she must find a way to pass the time. Whether she cares for mortals, enjoys watching, or serves a plan is unknown. Do not give her a motive.

132.comment: Istaroth's Intentions: Direidyth and the Key
132.content: Direidyth was a Khaenri'ahn girl from the time of the Cataclysm who believed in the Savior. According to the wiki, she became caught in a superimposition of Khaenri'ah over Natlan created through Istaroth when the sibling activated the Loom of Fate. She met the Traveler there, and her account to the sibling in her own time led the sibling to leave Khaenri'ah to find the Traveler. In A Space and Time Without You, the sibling says Istaroth must have had a hand in it and asks whether she is mocking them. No reason is given.

133.content: Istaroth gave Zibai a Moon Wheel and later warned her that blocking the Celestial Nail over Lang-Gan would defy the Heavenly Principles and cost her life. Zibai blocked it so that her people could flee. Istaroth then froze her at the moment of death and sealed her soul in Ziju, Zizhi and Zijiao. The reason for the rescue is not given.

134.comment: Istaroth's Intentions: Sacred Sakura Higher Power
134.content: Ei believes Makoto's plan to plant the Sacred Sakura through time could not have worked without a higher power, which the wiki identifies as Istaroth. Whether Makoto knew, and what Istaroth gained, is unstated.

135.content:
King Deshret's Civilization (also: King Deshret's kingdom, Deshret's kingdom, Kingdom of King Deshret, Deshret's civilisation, Akhtamun): King Deshret's civilization was the desert kingdom of ancient Sumeru, ruled by the god-king Deshret, Lord of Deserts, alongside two companion gods: Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers, and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, the earlier Dendro Archon. After Nabu Malikata's death Deshret ruled the desert alone and pursued a utopia, Aaru, where no one would suffer age, hunger or loss. His research into forbidden knowledge destroyed his royal city and ravaged his people. He died sealing the disaster. Today's Eremites descend from his subjects, and Aaru Village and the ruins of the Great Red Sand preserve his legacy.

The kingdom's remains dominate southern Sumeru: the Mausoleum of King Deshret, Khaj-Nisut, Primal Constructs, Jinn lore and the unfinished afterlife Aaru. Because Aaru was reprogrammed after the burning of Irminsul (Archon Quest Song of the Welkin Moon, Act X "Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana", Version 6.6), his work now holds the world's stored memory in place of the old world tree.

Established: - Deshret was Lord of Deserts and one of the Three Eternal Companion-Gods, with Nabu Malikata and Rukkhadevata. He died thousands of years ago, in the Archon War era.
- He wanted an eternal paradise for his people and turned to forbidden knowledge, which polluted the desert.
- He gave his life to stop the disaster, while Rukkhadevata nearly exhausted her own power helping (Nahida, Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies).

- **The three gods.** The three ruled together as oathbound friends. Legend gives each a domain: the banquet to Nabu Malikata, authority to Deshret, life to Rukkhadevata. The wiki says this period was remembered as peaceful and prosperous, and that Deshret and Nabu Malikata built the city of Ay-Khanoum, "City of the Moon Maiden" in the Jinn tongue.
- **The split.** Deshret's ambition was great enough to defy the Heavenly Principles. Rukkhadevata would not join the plans and left to build her own civilization in the rainforest. Nabu Malikata died, and Deshret grieved; he used the power of a Celestial Nail of the sands and the Jinn to raise the Eternal Oasis as her resting place, guarded by Ferigees.
- **His rule.** Alone, Deshret sought vassal-kings and priests with incorrupt hearts and founded a royal city, Akhtamun. He was called the master of the thousand and one Jinn and "king of warriors, horticulturists and sages", and was also known as the Mourning King for his grief and nostalgia.
- **Apep.** Before building his kingdom he struck a bargain with the Dendro Dragon Apep, who claimed the desert: she would leave his people in peace if she could consume him after his death and take his knowledge.
- **Gurabad.** The city of brass rose in the desert after Nabu Malikata's death and is tied, in different accounts, to Deshret's guidance. Liloupar engineered its destruction; Deshret, enraged, had her spirit split into seven parts and hidden by his seven sages.
- **Aaru and the fall.** After Gurabad he doubled down on a plan for Aaru, an artificial afterlife for desert dwellers, made possible by the knowledge from Celestia that Nabu Malikata had given him. Accounts of her death differ: one says the Heavenly Principles executed her for this transgression, another that she gave her life in a ritual so he could receive that knowledge. His forbidden research released the knowledge that became the Withering; Rukkhadevata aided him, temples of life-power were raised, and Deshret finally sacrificed himself. Apep ate his body as agreed and was corrupted.

Accounts: - **Nahida** presents the disaster as forbidden knowledge polluting the desert, repelled thanks to Deshret's self-sacrifice and Rukkhadevata's near-exhaustion.
- **Apep** holds that Deshret meant her corruption as a fail-safe and says she thought little of him, though other texts call her his friend.
- **Ormazd** credited Deshret for Gurabad's prosperity and honoured him with temples, while **Liloupar** says Deshret charged Gurabad to guard the Eternal Oasis; other accounts credit Liloupar and say Ferigees defied Deshret.
- **Eremites** remember him as a god-king to restore.

Open questions: - Where Deshret came from, and when exactly his kingdom rose and fell.
- Whether Nabu Malikata returned his love.
- How much of Gurabad was his doing.
- Whether he foresaw Apep's corruption.

Connections: - Related entries: Nabu Malikata and Rukkhadevata (companion gods), Aaru and Irminsul (the afterlife and world-memory system), forbidden knowledge and the Withering, the Archon War, the Eremites and Aaru Village (present-day descendants).
- Do not merge with the Unified Civilization of the first era; the wiki's placement of Deshret after the funerary war is an inference.

136.content: Aaru is the unfinished artificial afterlife Deshret designed for desert dwellers so they could escape the dangers of Teyvat and its gods. Long closed off and unfinished, it held three imprisoned Pillars. After Nahida burned the corrupted Irminsul with the Pyro Gnosis in the Archon Quest act Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana (Version 6.6), Aaru was reprogrammed to store the ley lines' information. The wiki adds that the Heavenly Principles lost direct control over fate as a result.

137.comment: King Deshret's Civilization: Akhtamun and Ay-Khanoum
137.content: Akhtamun is the royal city Deshret founded in the desert and the place his forbidden research destroyed. Ay-Khanoum, "City of the Moon Maiden" in the Jinn language, is the older city he and Nabu Malikata built together; the wiki later records it as one of the Cities of the Seven Towers.

138.comment: King Deshret's Civilization: Deshret's Seven Pillars
138.content: Deshret's court of chief servants. Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf were locked in Aaru until the three questions were answered; Nefer's answer, "time", freed them in the Version 6.6 Archon Quest, and they agreed to unseal Aaru's Shut so Sumeru could modify it.

139.content: The wiki traces the Withering, and its human form Eleazar, to the forbidden knowledge Deshret unleashed. Rukkhadevata aided him with temples of life-power, but the threat persisted until his death temporarily ended it. See the forbidden knowledge entry for what that knowledge is.

140.content:
Archon Quest (Overall Premise) (also: Archon Quest, Archon Quests, Genshin main story, the Traveler's journey): The Archon Quest is Teyvat's main story. Twin travellers from another world try to leave Teyvat, and an unknown god (later named as Asmoday) blocks their way. She takes one twin and seals the other, the Traveler. On waking, the Traveler fishes the floating companion Paimon out of the sea, and the two cross the nations in turn: Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru, Fontaine, Natlan, then Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya. In each, they meet that nation's Archon, one of The Seven, hoping the gods know where the lost twin is. In Liyue they learn the twin now leads the Abyss Order in a war against the gods. From then on the journey is also about understanding why.

Two threads run through every chapter. The Fatui, servants of the Tsaritsa, collect the Archons' Gnoses. The fallen kingdom of Khaenri'ah and its Cataclysm, about 500 years ago, link the sibling, Dainsleif, the hilichurls and the Harbingers. As of 7.1 the Traveler and Paimon are in Snezhnaya, the last nation of the twin's journey.

Established: Players choose which twin they play, so the Traveler is Aether and the sibling Lumine, or the reverse. Paimon is the guide and constant companion. The Traveler needs no Vision. They take up each nation's element, mostly by resonating with its Statue of The Seven. In Mondstadt, Venti remarks that he knew the Tsaritsa well five hundred years ago, but that after a catastrophe at that time she cut off all ties with him. That is the first hint of the Cataclysm.

Structure: Story order (release versions): Prologue, Mondstadt (1.0); Chapter I, Liyue (1.0-1.4); Chapter II, Inazuma (1.6-2.6); Chapter III, Sumeru (3.0-3.5); Chapter IV, Fontaine (4.0-4.7); Chapter V, Natlan (5.0-5.7); Song of the Welkin Moon, Nod-Krai and later Sumeru (5.8-6.6); Chapter VII, "Everwinter Without Mercy", Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, after "A Rekviem for the Underworld", the Traveler and Paimon are in Snezhnaya, on cooperative terms with the Tsaritsa and the Fatui. Ronova has lost her Authority and is dying. Before her end she made a Nail of Retribution crumble, which threatens to release Holy Soil. The sibling has not been found. The story has not yet reached Khaenri'ah.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (this project's advice): what characters know depends on where a scene falls in this order. Most residents never learn Archon Quest secrets. A default "present day" scene is set after 7.1.

key: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind
141.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Prologue and Chapter I
141.content:
Prologue (Mondstadt, 1.0). The dragon Dvalin, called Stormterror, attacks Mondstadt after the Abyss Order poisons him and turns him against it. The bard Venti is Barbatos, the Anemo Archon. With the Knights of Favonius, Venti and the Traveler free Dvalin. Afterwards the Harbinger Signora tears Venti's Gnosis out of him for the Tsaritsa, and Venti sends the Traveler on to Liyue.

Chapter I (Liyue). Rex Lapis is found dead at the Rite of Descension, and the Traveler is suspected. Tartaglia (Childe) leads them to Zhongli. The Fatui free the sealed god Osial, and Ningguang crushes him with her Jade Chamber. Zhongli then reveals he is Morax. He staged his death to test Liyue, and under a contract with the Tsaritsa he gives his Gnosis to Signora.

key: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana
142.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Chapters II and III
142.content:
Chapter II (Inazuma). Under the Sakoku and Vision Hunt Decrees, the Traveler joins the Watatsumi resistance. The Fatui arm both sides and give the rebels Delusions that kill their users. Teppei dies of one. The Traveler defeats Signora in a duel, and the Shogun executes her. Then they persuade Ei, inside the Plane of Euthymia, to give up her rigid Eternity. Yae Miko had given the Electro Gnosis to the Harbinger Scaramouche to keep the Traveler safe.

Chapter III (Sumeru). The sages had imprisoned Nahida for 500 years, and with Dottore they try to make a god from Scaramouche and the Electro Gnosis. The Traveler and allies free Nahida and defeat the false god. Nahida cleanses Irminsul of forbidden knowledge. Only the Traveler remembers Rukkhadevata. Dottore leaves with the Electro and Dendro Gnoses.

key: A Space and Time for You
143.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Chapters IV and V
143.content:
Chapter IV (Fontaine). A prophecy says the seas will rise and every Fontainian will dissolve. Furina is revealed to be a human who played the Hydro Archon for 500 years so the god Focalors could have herself judged and executed. That returned the Hydro Authority to Neuvillette, who later gives the Hydro Gnosis to Arlecchino.

Chapter V (Natlan). Mavuika, the Pyro Archon, leads Natlan's war against the Abyss with heroes who hold Ancient Names. The Traveler receives the Ancient Name "Tumaini". The Pyro statue would not respond to the Traveler; the Lord of the Night grants them Pyro instead. The Harbinger Capitano first opposes Mavuika, then allies with her and gives his life in her place. He had asked the Tsaritsa to relieve him of the mission to take the Pyro Gnosis, and she agreed.

144.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Song of the Welkin Moon in the main story
144.content: Song of the Welkin Moon (5.8-6.6). Varka invites the Traveler to Nod-Krai. There Columbina, the former Third Harbinger, opposes Dottore, who seizes the power of the moons. He is defeated. Columbina takes the Traveler to their crashed ship on the Frost Moon and loosens Teyvat's restrictions on their use of the elements. In the final Sumeru acts, Dottore attacks from inside Irminsul. Nahida burns Irminsul with the Pyro Gnosis, and Dottore dies.

145.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Chapter VII in the main story
145.content: Chapter VII (Snezhnaya, 7.0-7.1). Paimon falls ill on arrival. The Traveler gains Cryo and joins the secret society Rokot. Ronova, the Shade of Death, enforces a "Curse of Death" whenever Snezhnaya's research threatens Celestia, and she wants Paimon. Pierro reveals he pulled Paimon from Celestia to Khaenri'ah more than 500 years ago. The Traveler sides with Snezhnaya to protect her. The Tsaritsa (Anastasya) ends all investigations into the Traveler and explains that she gathers Gnoses to face the Heavenly Principles.

146.content: The Traveler takes up each nation's element: Anemo in Mondstadt, Geo in Liyue, Electro in Inazuma, Dendro in Sumeru, Hydro in Fontaine and Cryo in Snezhnaya, mostly by resonating with a Statue of The Seven. In Natlan the Pyro statue did not respond, and the Lord of the Night granted Pyro during the final battle against the Abyss.

147.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Where the Gnoses went
147.content: Signora took the Anemo Gnosis from Venti (1.0) and received Geo from Zhongli (1.1). Electro went from Yae Miko to Scaramouche, then to Dottore. Dendro went from Nahida to Dottore (3.2). Hydro went from Neuvillette to Arlecchino (4.2). The Pyro mission was cancelled, and Mavuika's Pyro Gnosis burned with Irminsul and vanished (6.6). In 7.1 the Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses, including her own Cryo Gnosis, and uses them to manipulate time and space.

key: fates that will not come to pass
148.content:
